After instilling, his soles, neck, palms, ears etc. should be massaged- mildly, he should then turn to his sides and spit out till the entire medicine comes out. In this manner two or three nasal medications should be administered to him. If he goes unconscious, cold water should be sprinkled over the face, avoiding head. Nasal medication with fat material should be given at the end of purgative Nasal medications, in consideration of the Doshas etc. After medication is completed, the patient should lie with face upwards, for a period of uttering one hundred syllables (for 100 seconds), Then he should inhale smoke of medicated herbs and gargle the month with lukewarm water many times to cleanse the throat. (remember that Marsha and Pratimarsha are the two types of Sneha nasya) Sukha Uchvasa – Expiration without difficulty, Sukha swapna – sleep, Sukha bodha – easy awakening from sleep and Akshapatava – keenness of sense organs are the signs of lubricating nasal therapy properly done. Akshi stabdhata – Loss of movement of the eyes, Shosha Nasa asye – emaciation, dryness of the nose and mouth, Murdha shunyata – feeling of emptiness inside the head are the signs of dryness- or inadequate Lubrication. Kandu – Itching, Guruta – feeling of heaviness of the head, Praseka – excess salivation, Aruchi – anorexia, Peenasa – rhinitis are signs of excess of Lubrications therapy. Akshikaghuta – lightness of the eyes, Vaktra swara vishuddhi – clean mouth and clear voice; Inadequate Virechana Nasya (purgative therapy ) causes exacerbation of the diseases and excess therapy leads to emaciation.

sanskrit_text: प्रतिमर्शः क्षतक्षामबालवृद्धसुखात्मसु प्रयोज्यो अकालवर्षेऽपि न त्विष्टो दुष्टपीनसे मद्यपीते अबलश्रोत्रे कृमिदूषितमूर्धनि उत्क्लिष्टोत्क्लिष्टदोषे च, हीनमात्रतया हि सः २६-२७ निशाहर्भुक्त्वान्ताहः स्वप्नाध्वश्रमरेतसाम् शिरोअभ्यञ्जनगण्डूषप्रस्रावाञ्जनवर्चसाम् ॥२८॥ दन्तकाष्ठस्य हासस्य योज्यो अन्ते असौ द्विबिन्दुकः । पञ्चसु स्रोतसां शुद्धिः, क्लमनाशस्त्रिषु क्रमात् दृग्बलं पञ्चसु, ततो दन्तदार्ढ्यं मरुच्छमः २९ न नस्यमूनसप्ताब्दे नातीताशीतिवत्सरे न चोनाष्टादशे धूमः, कवला नोनपञ्चमे न शुद्धिरूनदशमे न चान्तिक्रान्तसप्ततौ ३०-३१ आजन्ममरणं शस्तः प्रतिमर्शस्तु बस्तिवत् मर्शावच्च गुणान् कुर्यात्स हि नित्योपसेवनात् न चात्र यन्त्रणा नापि व्यापद्भयो मर्शवद्भयम् ३२ तैलमेव च नस्यार्थे नित्याभ्यासेन शस्यते ॥३३॥ शिरसः श्लेष्मधामत्वात् स्नेहाः स्वस्थस्य नेतरे ।
transliteration: pratim arśaḥ kṣatakṣāmabālavṛddhasukhātmasu prayojyo akālavarṣe'pi na tviṣṭo duṣṭapīnase madyapīte abalaśrotre kṛmidūṣitamūrdhani utkliṣṭotkliṣṭadoṣe ca, hīnamātratayā hi saḥ 26-27 niśāhar bhuktvāntāhaḥ svapnādhvaśramaretasām śiroabhyañjanagaṇḍūṣaprasrāvāñjanavarcasām ||28|| dantakāṣṭhasya hāsasya yojyo ante asau dvibindukaḥ | pañcasu srotasāṃ śuddhiḥ, klamanāśastriṣu kramāt dṛgbalaṃ pañcasu, tato dantadārḍhyaṃ marucchamaḥ 29 na nasyamūnasa ptābde nātītāśītivat sare na conāṣṭādaśe dhūmaḥ, kavalā nonapañcame na śuddhirūnadaśame na cāntikrāntasaptatau 30-31 ājanmamaraṇaṃ śastaḥ pratimarśastu bastivat marśāvacca guṇān kuryātsa hi nityopasevanāt na cātra yantraṇā nāpi vyāpadbhayo marśavadbhayam 32 tailameva ca nasyārthe nityābhyāsena śasyate ||33|| śirasaḥ śleṣmadhāmatvāt snehāḥ svasthasya netare |
commentary: Pratimarsha Nasya is a type of oil / fat Nasya. Here the dose is very low. Hence, it is indicated in wide variety of diseases. It can be administered to Kshata – wounded, Kshaama – the emaciated, Baala – the children, Vruddha – the aged and Sukhaatma – those who lead a happy conservative life; it can be administered even during unsuitable time, season, day etc. It can also be administered during rainy season. Contra indication for Pratimarsha nasya – It is not suitable in Dushta Peenasa – infective Rhinitis, Madyapeeta – those who has have drunk wine, Abalashrota – People with low ears- low hearing capacity, Krumidushita Murdha – head infested with worms, Utklishta Dosha – in whom, in the Doshas are greatly imbalanced and moving from place to place; In these conditions, it is not suitable because it is of less quantity. After head massage, After Gandusha (gargling), After Anjana – collyrium, After defecation, After tooth brushing, After bouts of laughing ; its dose is two Bindu- 2 drops. Pratimarsha cleanses, clears the channels, relieves fatigue, improves eye sight, bestows sturdiness to the teeth and mitigates the Vata. Nasya should not be administered to those who are less seven years and more than 80 years of age; Dhuma- inhalation of smoke of drugs should not be administered for children below 18 years; Kavala- mouth gargling should not be administered for children below five years; Shodhana – purification (Panchakarma) therapies like Vamana, Virechana etc. should not be administered below 10 years and above 70 years of age. Pratimarsha – kind of nasal medication is good from birth to death just like basti treatment. It provides the benefits like Marsha Nasya (oil, high dose if used daily, it does not need any control – regarding food and activities nor it has any risks like Marsha Nasya. Medicated oil only is ideal for daily use of Nasya (Pratimarsha), because the head is the dwelling place of kapha and no fat other than oil, can keep it healthy.

sanskrit_text: आशुकृच्चिरकारित्वं गुणोत्कर्षापकृष्टता मर्शं च प्रतिमर्शं च विशेषो न भवेद्यदि को मर्शं सपरीहारं सापदं च भजेत्ततः अच्छपानविचाराख्यौ कुटीवातातपस्थिती अन्वासामात्राबस्ती च तद्वदेव विनिर्दिशेत् ३४-३६ जीवन्तीजलदेवदारुजलदत्वक्सेव्यगोपीहिमं दार्वीत्वङ्मधुकप्लवागुरुवरीपुण्ड्राह्वबिल्वोत्पलम् धावन्यौ सुरभिं स्थिरे कृमिहरं पत्रं तृटि रेणुकां किञ्जल्कं कमलाद्बलां शतगुणे दिव्ये अम्भसि क्वाथयेत् ३७ तैलाद्रसं दशगुणं परिशोष्य तेन तैलं पचेत् सलिलेन दशैव वारान् पाके क्षिपेच्चदशमे सममाजदुग्धं नस्यं महागुणमुशन्त्यणुतैलमेतत् ३८ घनोन्नतप्रसन्नत्वक्स्कन्धग्रीवास्यवक्षसः दृढेन्द्रियास्तपलिता भवेयुर्नस्यशीलिनः ३९
transliteration: āśukṛccirakāritvaṃ guṇotkarṣāpakṛṣṭatā marśaṃ ca pratimarśaṃ ca viśeṣo na bhavedyadi ko marśaṃ saparīhāraṃ sāpadaṃ ca bhajettataḥ acchapānavicārākhyau kuṭīvātātapasthitī anvāsāmātrāb bastī ca tadvadeva vinirdiśet 34-36 jīvantījaladevadārujaladatvaksevyagopīhimaṃ dārvītvaṅmadhukaplavāguruv arīpuṇḍrāhvabilvotpalam dhāvanyau surabhiṃ sthira kṛmiharaṃ patraṃ tṛṭi reṇukāṃ kiñjalkaṃ kamalādbalāṃ śataguṇe divye ambhasi kvāthayet 37 tailādrasaṃ daśaguṇaṃ pariśoṣya tena tailaṃ pacet salilena daśaiva vārān pāke kṣipec cadaśame samamājadugdhaṃ nasyaṃ mahāguṇamuśantyṇutailametat 38 ghanonnataprasannatvakskandhagrīvāsyavakṣasaḥ dṛḍhendriyāstapalitā bhaveyurnasyaśīlinaḥ 39
commentary: Immediate and delayed action, more and less benefits are the results of Marsha and Pratimarsa respectively. If there is no difference between then, who will resort to marsha which is associated with controls – regarding food and activities and risks? In the same way, Acchapana – drinking of pure fat alone and Vicharana- intake of fat mixed with foods etc. Similar is the case of Kuti Pravesika – one kind of rejuvenation therapy where the person needs to stay in a house for weeks together, taking Chyawanprash etc. and Vatatapika- Rejuvenation treatment, wherein patient can do his routine work. Similar is the case of Anuvasana – fat enema and Matra basti – fat enema with very little oil. Jivanti, Jala, Devadaru, Jalada, Twak, Sevya, Gopi (sariva), Hima, Darvi twak, Madhuka, Plava, Agaru, Shatavari, Pundrahva, Bilva, Utpala, the two Dhavani, surabhi, the two Sthira, Krmihara (Vidanga), Patram (Cinnamon leaf), Truti (Cardamom), Renuka, Kinjalka, Kamala (lotus) and Bala- are to be boiled in one hundred parts of rain water / pure water and decoction reduced to one tenth part; to this decoction, equal quantity of sesame oil is added and cooked for ten times. (the decoction is added to the oil, boiled till water evaporation. Again, equal quantity of decoction is added, evaporated. This process is repeated for 10 times. During the tenth cooking, equal quantity of goats milk (equal to the quantity of oil) is added – and cooking is completed. This oil known as Anutaila, used as nasal drops, bestows great benefits. The skin, shoulders, neck face and chest become thick, well developed and bright; The body parts and the sense organs become strong, disappearance of grey hairs will be obtained by persons who becomes habituated to nasal medication.

sanskrit_text: जत्रूर्ध्वकफवातोत्थविकाराणामजन्मने उच्छेदाय च जातानां पिबेद्धूमं सदात्मवान् १ स्निग्धो मध्यः स तीक्ष्णश्च वाते वातकफे कफे योज्यः
transliteration: jatrūrdhvakaphavātott hav ikārāṇāmajanmane ucchhedāya ca jātānāṃ pibeddhūmaṃ sadātmavān 1 snigdho madhyaḥ sa tīkṣṇaśca vāte vātakaphe kaphe yojyaḥ
commentary: The person who wishes to take care of his health should inhale herbal smoke daily to treat or to prevent the onset of diseases of the parts above the shoulders, arising from – increases of kapha and Vata. Snigdha Dhuma – lubricating, also known as Mrudu (Soft) / Prayogika – useful in Vata imbalance. Madhya Dhuma – medium – useful in Vata and Kapha imbalance. Also known as Shamana Dhuma. Teekshna Dhuma – strong, useful in Kapha imbalance. Also known as Virechana dhuma (Purifying).

sanskrit_text: न रक्तपित्तार्तिविरिक्तोदरमेहिषु तिमिरोर्ध्वानिलाध्मानरोहिणीदत्तबस्तिषु मत्स्यमद्यदधिक्षीरक्षौद्रस्नेहविषाशिषु शिरस्याभिहते पाण्डुरोगे जागरिते निशि २-४ रक्तपित्तान्ध्यबाधिर्यतृण्मूर्च्छामदमोहकृत् ॥४॥ धूमो अकाले अतिपीतो वा तत्र शीतविधिर्हित: ५
transliteration: na raktapittārtiviriktodaramehiṣu timirordhvānilādhmānarohiṇīdattabastiṣu matsyamadyadadhikṣīrakṣaudrasnehaviṣāśiṣu śirasyābhi hate pāṇḍuroge jāgarite niśi 2-4 raktapittāndhyabādhiryatṛṇmūrcchāmadamohakṛt ||4|| dhūmo akāle atipīto vā tatra śītavidhirhitaḥ 5
commentary: Inhalation of smoke should not be done for persons who are suffering from Raktapitta- bleeding disease, Virikta – who has undergone Virechana therapy, Udara – ascites, intestinal obstruction, Meha – diabetes, urinary tract disorders, Timira – blindness, Urdhwa Anila – upward movement of Vata, Adhmana – Flatulence, bloating, Rohini- a serious disease of the throat, diphtheria, Datta Basti – who have been administered enema, who have just eaten fish, wine, curds, milk, honey, fats and poison; who are injured in the head, Pandu- anemia and Jagarita – those who have kept awake at night. Doing Dhumapana at improper time or in excess leads to Rakta pitta- bleeding disease, Andhya – blindness, Badhirya – deafness, Trut – excessive thirst, Murcha – fainting, loss of consciousness, Mada, Moha – delusion. For this cold regimen should be adopted.

sanskrit_text: क्षुतजृम्भितविण्मूत्रस्त्रीसेवाशस्त्रकर्मणाम् हासस्य दन्तकाष्ठस्य धूममन्ते पिबेन्मृदुम् ५ कालेष्वेषु निशाहारनावनान्ते च मध्यमम् निद्रानस्योञ्जनस्नानच्छर्दितान्ते विरेचनम् ६ बस्तिनेत्रसमद्रव्यं त्रिकोशं कारयेदृजु मूलाग्रेऽङ्गुष्ठकोलास्थिप्रवेशं धूमनेत्रकम् ७ तीक्ष्णस्नेहनमध्येषु त्रीणि चत्वारि पञ्च च अङ्गुलानां क्रमात्पातुः प्रमाणे नाष्टकानि तत् ८
transliteration: kṣutajṛmbhitaviṇmūtrastrīsevāśastrakarmaṇām hāsasya dantakāṣṭhasya dhūmamante pibenmṛdum 5 kāleṣveṣu niśāhāranāvanānte ca madhyamam nidrānasyoñjanasnānaccharditānte virecanam 6 bastinetrasamadravyaṃ trikośaṃ kārayedṛju mūlāgre'ṅguṣṭhakolāsthipraveśaṃ dhūmanetrakam 7 tīkṣṇasnehanamadhyeṣu trīṇi catvāri pañca ca aṅgulānāṃ kramātpātuḥ pramāṇe nāṣṭakāni tat 8
commentary: Mild, lubricating smoke should be inhaled at the end of sneezing, yawing, defecation, urination, copulation, surgical operation, bouts of laughing, use of tooth brush. Medium strength smoke should be inhaled at the end of the night, end of the meals and end of Nasya therapy. Purgative, strong smoke should be inhaled at the end of sleep, at the end of Nasya treatment, After applying collyrium, After bath and After vomiting. The smoke apparatus should be prepared from the same material as of enema nozzle (from metals like gold, silver, iron etc); It should have three chambers, It should be straight, It should permit the entry of the thumb and a Kolasthi- seed of jujube fruit through orifices at its root and tip respectively. The length of the tube should be 24 Angula (width of one knuckle) for Mrudu (soft, Sneha) Dhuma, 32 Angula for medium Dhuma and 40 Angula for strong Virechana Dhuma.

topic_heading: Dhumapana Vidhi, Dhuma Dravyani and Dhumavarti
sanskrit_text: ऋजूपविष्ट विवृतास्यस्त्रिपर्ययम् पिधाय च्छिद्रमेकैकं धूमं नासिकया पिबेत् प्राक् पिबेन्नासयोत्क्लिष्टे दोषे घ्राणशिरोगते उत्क्लेशनार्थं वक्त्रेण, विपरीतं तु कण्ठगे नासया द्रिग्विघातकृत् ९-११ आक्षेपमोक्षैः पातव्यो धूमस्तु त्रिभिस्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः अहनः पिबेत्सकृत्स्निग्धं, द्विर्मध्यं, शोधनं परम् त्रिश्चतुर्वा १२ मृदौ तत्र द्रव्याण्यगुरुगुग्गुलु मुस्तस्थौणेयशैलेयनलदोशीरवालकम् वयङ्गकौन्तीमधुकबिल्वमज्जैलवालुकम् श्रीवेष्टकं सर्जरसो ध्यामकं मदनं प्लवम् शल्लकी कुंकुमं माषा यवाः कुन्दुरुकास्तिलाः स्नेहः फलानां साराणां मेदो मज्जा वसा घृतम् १३-१५ शमने शल्लकी लाक्षा पृथ्वीका कमलोत्पलम् न्यग्रोधोदुम्बराश्वत्थप्लक्षरोध्रत्वचः सिताः यष्टिमधु स्वर्णत्वक् पद्मकं रक्तयष्टिका गन्धाश्चाकुष्ठतगराः १६ तीक्ष्णे ज्योतिष्मती निशा दशमूलमानोह्वालं लाक्षा श्वेता फलत्रयम् गन्धद्रव्याणि तीक्ष्णानि गणो मूर्धविरेचनः १७-१८ जले स्थितामहोरात्रमीषिकां द्वादशाङ्गुलाम् पिष्टैर्धूमौषधैरेवम् पञ्चकृत्वः प्रलेपयेत् वर्तिरङ्गुष्ठकस्थूलो यवमध्या यथा भवेत् छायाशुष्कां विगर्भां तां स्नेहाभ्यक्तां यथायथम् धूमनेत्रापिहितां पातुमग्निप्लुष्टां प्रयोजयेत् १९-२० शरावसम्पुटच्छिद्रे नाडीं न्यस्य दशाङ्गुलाम् अष्टाङ्गुलां वा वक्त्रेण कासवान् धूममापिबेत् २१
transliteration: ṛjūpaviṣṭa vivṛtāsyastriparyayam pidhāya cchidramekaikaṃ dhūmaṃ nāsikayā pibet prāk pibennāsayotkliṣṭe doṣe ghrāṇaśirogate utkleśanārthaṃ vaktreṇa, viparītaṃ tu kaṇṭhage nāsayā drigvighātakṛt 9-11 ākṣepamokṣaiḥ pātavyo dhūmastu tribhistribhistribhiḥ ahanaḥ pibetsakṛtsnigdhaṃ, dvirmadhyaṃ, śodhanaṃ param triścaturvā 12 mṛdau tatra dravyāṇyaguruguggulu mustasthauneyaśaileyanaladośīravālakam vayaṅgakountīmadhukabilvamajjailavālukam śrīveṣṭakaṃ sarjaraso dhyāmakaṃ madanaṃ plavam shallakī kuṃkumaṃ māṣā yavāḥ kundurukāstilāḥ snehaḥ phalānāṃ sārāṇāṃ medo majjā vasā ghṛtam 13-15 śamane shallakī lākṣā pṛthvīkā kamalotpalam nyagrodhodumbarāśvatthaplakṣarodhratvacaḥ sitāḥ yaṣṭimadhu svarṇatvak padmakaṃ raktayaṣṭikā gandhāścākuṣṭhatagarāḥ 16 tīkṣṇe jyotiṣmatī niśā daśamūlamānohvālaṃ lākṣā śvetā phalatrayam gandhadravyāṇi tīkṣṇāṇi gaṇo mūrdhavirecanaḥ 17-18 jale sthitāmahorātramīṣikāṃ dvādaśāṅgulām piṣṭairdhūmauṣadhair evaṃ pañcakṛtvaḥ pralepayet vartiraṅguṣṭhaka sthūlo yavamadhyā yathā bhavet chāyāśuṣkāṃ vigarbhāṃ tāṃ snehābhyaktāṃ yathāyatham dhūmanetrāpihitāṃ pātumagnipluṣṭāṃ prayojayet 19-20 śarāvasaṃpuṭacchidre nāḍīṃ nyasya daśāṅgulām aṣṭāṅgulāṃ vā vakt reṇa kāsavān dhūmamāpibet 21
commentary: The patient should sit straight, attentive, with his mouth open and inhale the smoke through each nostril alternatively, While inhaling from one nostril, he should close the other. Inhalation should be done thrice – inhaling the smoke and letting it out together form one bout; three such bouts should be done each time. Smoke should be inhaled through the nose first if the imbalanced Doshas are localized in the nose and head. If Dosha from nose and head are not coming out, but are adhering, inhalation should be done first through the mouth to make them move; and later through the nose. When the Doshas are localized in the throat – inhalation should be done in reverse order- first by the nose and later by the mouth. The smoke inhaled (either from mouth or from nose) should be let out only through the mouth; if let out through the nose, it produces loss of vision. Smoking should be done thrice, with three times inhaling and three exhaling alternately. Snigdha- lubricating, mild kind of smoke should be taken for only set of three inhalation and exhalations, during day time. Madhya- medium kind – two sets of 3 inhales and exhales and Shodhana- purgative, strong kind, 3 – 4 sets of 3 inhales and exhales. For Mridu- mild kind of smoke, useful drugs are-Aguru, Guggulu, Musta, sthauneya, Shaileya, Nalada, Usheera, Valaka, Varanga, Kounti, Madhuka, Bilvamajja, elavaluka, Shrivestaka, Sarjarasa, Dhyamaka, Madana, Plava, Shallaki, Kumkuma, Masha, Yava, Kunduruka, Tila, oil obtained from fruits and pith of trees, fat, Marrow, muscle- fat and ghee. For Shamana- Madyama, medium kind of smoke, useful drugs are - shallaki, Laksha,Prithvika, Kamala, Utpala, Barks of Nyagrodha, Udumbara, Asvattha, Plaksa and Rodhra; Sita, Yasthimadhu (licorice), Suvarnatwak, Padmaka, Raktayastika, Kustha, tagara and other scents – perfumeries. For Teekshna – strong, Purgative kind of smoke, useful drugs are Jyotismati, Nisha (turmeric), Dashamula, Ala, Laksa, Shweta, Triphala, Substances which have strong smell and drugs of Murdha Virechana Gana- vide chapter 15. A reed (tall, grass like plant), twelve Angula in length, soaked in water for a day and night, should be wrapped in five layers-one over the other with a ribbon of cloth; it is smeared with thin paste of drugs, its thickness being that of the middle portion of the thumb. It should be dried in shade, removed of its reed, smeared with any suitable fat material (oil / ghee). It should be inserted into the smoking tube, lit with fire and the smoke is inhaled. A tube either 10 or 8 Angula in length should be fixed to a hole made in a capsule of earthen saucers and the person suffering from cough made to inhale smoke – through the tube. Notes- A burning coal / charcoal is placed inside an earthen pot. Powder of herbs is sprinkled over it and covered with another vessel, having a hole at its center. A tube is connected to the hole, through which the smoke is inhaled.

sanskrit_text: कासः श्वासः पीनसो विस्वरत्वं पूतिर्गन्धः पाण्डुता केशदोषः कर्णस्याक्षिस्रावकण्डुवर्तिजाड्यं तन्द्रा हिध्मा धूमपं न स्पृशन्ति २२
transliteration: kāsaḥ śvāsaḥ pīnasaḥ visvaratvaṃ pūtirgandhaḥ pāṇḍutā keśadoṣaḥ karṇasyākṣisrāvakaṇḍuvartijāḍyaṃ tandrā hidhmā dhūmapaṃ na spṛśanti 22
commentary: Cough, Dyspnoea, Rhinitis, Disorders of voice, bad smell – of the nose and mouth, pallor of the face, disorders of hairs; discharges, itching, pain and in activities – diminution or loss of function of the ears, mouth and eyes; stupor and hiccup do not affect the person who inhales smoke- habitually.

sanskrit_text: चतुष्प्रकारो गण्डूषः स्निग्धः शमनशोधनौ रोपणश्च त्रयस्तत्र त्रिषु योज्याश्चलादिषु १ अन्त्यो व्रणघ्नः स्निग्धो अत्र स्वाद्वम्लपटुसाधितैः स्नेहैः संशमनः तिक्तकषायमधुरौषधैः २ शोधनः तिक्तकट्वम्लपटूष्णैः रोपणः पुनः कषायतिक्तकैः ३
transliteration: catuṣprakāro gaṇḍūṣaḥ snigdhaḥ śamanaśodhanau ropaṇaśca trayastatra triṣu yojyāścalādiṣu 1 antyo vraṇaghnaḥ snigdho atra svādvamlapaṭusādhitaiḥ snehaiḥ saṃśamanaḥ tiktakaṣāyamadhurauṣadhaiḥ 2 śodhanaḥ tiktakaṭvamlapaṭūṣṇaiḥ ropaṇaḥ punaḥ kaṣāyatiktakaiḥ 3
commentary: Gandusha is of four kinds, viz – Snigdha – lubricating, with oils and fats – for Vata imbalance disorder, Shamana – palliative – for Pitta imbalance disorder, Shodhana – purifying – for Kapha imbalance disorder, Ropana – healing. Lubricating full mouth gargle is by the use of oil processed with herbs of sweet, sour and salt tastes. Palliative full mouth gargle is by herbs of bitter, astringent and sweet tastes. Purifying full gargle is with herbs of bitter, pungent, sour, salt tastes and possessing Ushna – hot property. Healing full gargle is with herbs of astringent and bitter.

sanskrit_text: तत्र स्नेहः क्षीरं मधूदकम् शुक्तं मद्यं रसो मूत्रं धान्याम्लं च यथायथम् कल्कैर्युक्तं विपक्वं वा यथास्पर्शं प्रयोजयेत् ४ तिलकल्कोदकं दन्तहर्षदन्तचालमुखरोगेषु वातिकेषु शस्तं शीतं वोष्णं वा ५ नित्यं तैलं मांसरसोऽथवा ऊषादाहान्विते पाके क्षते चागन्तुसम्भवे विषे क्षाराग्निदग्धे च सर्पिर्धार्यं पयोऽथवा ६ वैशद्यं जनयत्याशु सन्दधाति मुखे व्रणान् दाहतृष्णाप्रशमनं मधु गण्डूषधारणम् ७ धान्याम्लमास्यवैरस्य मलदौर्गन्ध्यनाशनम् तदेवालवणं शीतं मुखशोषहरं परम् आशु क्षाराम्बुगण्डूषो भिनत्ति श्लेष्मणश्चयम् सुखोष्णोदकगण्डूषैर्जायते वक्त्रलाघवम् ८-९
transliteration: tatra snehaḥ kṣīraṃ madhūdakam śuktaṃ madyaṃ raso mūtraṃ dhānyāmlaṃ ca yathāyatham kalkairyuktaṃ vipakvaṃ vā yathāsparśaṃ prayojayet 4 tilakalkodakaṃ dantaharṣadantacālamukharogeṣu vātikeṣu śastaṃ śītaṃ voṣṇaṃ vā 5 nityaṃ tailaṃ māṃsaraso'thavā ūṣādāhānvite pāke kṣate cāgantusambhave viṣe kṣārāgnidagdhe ca sarpirdhāryaṃ payo'thavā 6 vaiśadyaṃ janayatyāśu sandadhāti mukhe vraṇān dāhatṛṣṇāpraśamanaṃ madhu gaṇḍūṣadhāraṇam 7 dhānyāmlamāsyavairasya maladaurgandhyanāśanam tadevālavaṇaṃ śītaṃ mukhaśoṣaharaṃ param āśu kṣārām bugaṇḍūṣo bhinatti śleṣmaṇaścayam su khoṣṇodakagaṇḍūṣairjāyate vak tralāghavam 8-9
commentary: Fats – oil, ghee etc., milk, Honey with water, Shukta – fermented gruel, Madya – wine, Mamsarasa – juice of meat, Mutra – urine of animals or Dhanyamla – wash of grains fermented by keeping overnight, These liquids are commonly used in Gandusha. The liquids may be mixed with a kalka (herbal paste). The liquids may be cooked or raw. The liquids should be comfortable to touch and to hold in the mouth. In conditions like Dantaharsha – tingling of the teeth, Dantachala – shaky teeth, and disease of the mouth caused by Vata, Gandusha with water mixed with sesame seed paste – either lukewarm or cold, is useful. For daily use, either sesame oil or meat soup is good. When there is local or general burning sensation (Daha), ulceration and wounds caused by foreign bodies, poison wounds, alkalies (Kshara) and burns by fire, it is best to hold either ghee or milk. Honey - Holding honey in the mouth removes the sliminess of the mouth, heals the ulcers quickly, relieves burning sensation and thirst. Holding Dhanyamla – fermented grain wash in the mouth removes distaste, dirt (of teeth and tongue) and bad smell from the mouth. The same – Dhanyamla without salt, used cold, is best to remove dryness of the mouth. Holding Ksharambu – water containing alkalies in the mouth quickly breaks up the accumulation of Kapha. Holding comfortable warm water brings about lightness and cleansing of the mouth. The person should sit in a place devoid of breeze (Nivata) but in sunlight (Sa Aatapa). His shoulders and neck should be massaged and fomented; Keeping his face slightly lifted up, he should hold the liquid in his mouth till the mouth gets filled with Kapha or till the nose and eyes start secreting liquid.

sanskrit_text: निवाते सातपे स्विन्नमृदितस्कन्धकन्धरः १० गण्डूषमपिबन् किञ्जित् उन्नतास्यो विधारयेत् कफपूर्णास्यता यावत्स्रवद्घ्राणाक्षताअथवा ११ असञ्जार्यो मुखे पूर्णे गण्डूषः, कवलो अन्यथा मन्याशिरःकर्णमुखाक्षिरोगाः प्रसेककण्ठामयवक्त्रशोषाः १२ हृल्लासतन्द्रारुचिपीनसाश्च साध्या विशेषात्कवलग्रहणात् कल्को रसक्रिया चूर्णः त्रिविधं प्रतिसारणम् युञ्ज्यात्तत् कफरोगेषु गण्डूषविहितौषधैः १३ मुखलेपः त्रिधा दोषविषहा वर्णकृच्च सः १४ उष्णा वातकफे शस्तः, शेषेषु अत्यर्थशीतलः त्रिप्रमाणः चतुर्भाग त्रिभागार्ध्वाङ्गुलोन्नतिः १५ अशुष्कस्य स्थितिस्तस्य, शुष्को दूषयति छविम् तं आर्द्रयित्वा अपनयेत् तदन्ते अभ्यङ्ग आचरेत् १६ विवर्जयेद्दिवास्वप्नाभाष्याग्न्यातपशुक्क्रोधः न योज्यः पीनसे अजीर्णे दत्तनस्ये हनुग्रहे अरोचके जागरिते १७ स तु हन्ति सुयोजितः अकालपलितव्यङ्गवलीतिमिरनीलिकाः १८
transliteration: nivāte sātape svinnamṛditaskandhakandharaḥ 10 gaṇḍūṣamapiban kiñjit unnatāsyo vidhārayet kaphapūrṇāsyatā yāvatsravadghrāṇākṣatā athavā 11 asañjāryo mukhe pūrṇe gaṇḍūṣaḥ, kavalo anyathā manyāśiraḥkarṇamukhākṣir ogāḥ prasekakaṇṭhāmayavak traśoṣāḥ 12 hrllāsatandrārucipīnasāśca sādhyā viśeṣātkavalagrahaṇāt kalko rasakriyā cūrṇaḥ trividhaṃ pratisāraṇam yuñjyāttat kapharogeṣu gaṇḍūṣavihitauṣadhaiḥ 13 mukhalepaḥ tridhā doṣaviṣahā varṇakṛcca saḥ 14 uṣṇā vātakaphe śastaḥ, śeṣeṣu atyarthaśītalaḥ tripramāṇaḥ caturbhāga tribhāgārdhvāṅgulonnatiḥ 15 aśuṣkasya sthitistasya, śuṣko dūṣayati chavim taṃ ārdrayitvā apanayet tadante abhyaṅga ācaret 16 vivarjayeddivāsvapnābhāṣyāgnyātapaśuk krodhaḥ na yojyaḥ pīnase ajīrṇe dattanasye hanugrahe arocake jāgarite 17 sa tu hanti suyojitaḥ akālapalitavyaṅgavalītimiranīlikāḥ 18
commentary: Filling the mouth with liquids fully not permitting any movement inside is Gandusha. Taking liquid into mouth and moving it around by gargling for specific time period is Kavala. Diseases of the neck, head, ears, mouth and eyes, Praseka – excess salivation, diseases of the throat, dryness of the mouth, nausea, Tandra – stupor, Aruchi – anorexia and Peenasa – rhinitis are curable by Kavala – mouth gargles. Pratisarana – applying herbs to the interior of the mouth with the finger – is of three kinds, viz. Kalka – in the form of paste, Rasakriya – solidified decoction and Curna – powder. It should be done in diseases of Kapha origin with the same herbs as suggested for Gandusha. Mukhalepa – application of paste of herbs over the face is of three types – Doshaha – removing the Doshas, Vishaha – removing poison and Varnakara – improving complexion. It should be applied warm for Vata and Kapha and For Pitta imbalance, it should be cold. Its three thickness – Minimum – 1/4th Angula (Finger breadth), Medium – 1/3 Angula, Maximum – ½ Angula thickness. It should be allowed to remain till it becomes dry; when dry, it vitiates the skin colour, hence it should be removed soon after it becomes dry. While removing, it should be moistened for easy removal. After removal, a gentle oil massage should be given. The person should avoid day sleep, speaking for long hours, exposure to fire and sunlight, sorrow and anger during the procedure. It should not be administered to persons suffering from Peenasa – rhinitis, Ajeerna – indigestion, Nasya – who have received Nasya therapy, Hanugraha – locked jaw, Aruchi – anorexia, Jagarana – loss of sleep. If properly done, it cures Akalapalita – premature graying of hair, Vyanga – discolored patch on face, Vali – wrinkles, Timira – blindness and Neelika – bluish vision (a type of blindness).

sanskrit_text: कोलमज्जा वृषान्मूलशाबरगौरसर्षपाः सिंहीमूलं तिलाः कृष्णा दार्वीत्वङ्निस्तुषा यवाः दर्भमूलहिमोशीरशिरीषमिशितण्डुलाः कुमुदोत्पलकल्हारदूर्वामधुकचन्दनम् कालीयकतिलोशीरमांसीतगरपद्मकम् तालीसगुन्द्रापुण्ड्राह्वयष्टीकाशानतागुरु १९-२१ इत्यर्धार्धोदिता लेपा हेमन्तादिषु षट् स्मृताः मुखालेपनशीलानां दृढं भवति दर्शनम् वदनं चापरिम्लानं श्लक्ष्णं तामरसोपमम् २२
transliteration: kolamajjā vṛṣānmūlaśābaragaurasarṣapāḥ siṃhīmūlaṃ tilāḥ kṛṣṇā dārvītvaṅnistuṣā yavāḥ darbhamūlahimośīraśirīṣamiśitaṇḍulāḥ kumudotpalakalhāradūrvāmadhukacandanam kālīyakatilośīramāṃsītagarapadm akam tālīsagundrāpuṇḍrāhva yaṣṭīkāśānatāguru 19-21 ity ardhārdhoditā lepā hemantādiṣu ṣaṭ smṛtāḥ mukhalepanaśīlānāṃ dṛḍhaṃ bhavati darśanam vadanaṃ cāparimlānaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ tāmarasopamam 22
commentary: The following six recipes are ideal for the six seasons commencing with Hemanta –(early winter) respectively. For Hemanta (early winter) – Marrow of Kola, root of Vrisha (Vasa – Adhatoda vasica), Sabara and Gaurasarsapa (White mustard). For Shishira (winter) – Root of Simhi, Krisna tila (black sesame), bark of Darvi and Dehusked Yava (barley). For Vasantha (Spring) – Root of Darbha, Hima; Usheera, Shirisha, Mishi and Tandula (rice grains). For Greeshma (summer) – Kumuda, Utpala, Kalhara, Durva, Madhuka and Chandana (Sandalwood). For Varsha (Rainy season) – Kaliyaka, Tila, Usira, Mamsi, Tagara and Padmaka. For Sharath (Autumn) – Talisa, Gundra, Pundrahva, Yasti, Kasa, Nata and Aguru. For those who are habituated to application of paste of herbs on the face, the vision becomes keen, the face never dull, but smooth and brilliant resembling a lotus flower.

topic_heading: Murdha Taila – Oil treatment of the head
sanskrit_text: अभ्यङ्गसेकपिचवो बस्तिश्चेति चतुर्विधम् २३ मूर्धतैलम बहुगुणं तद्विद्यात् उत्तरोत्तरम् तत्राभ्यङ्गः प्रयोक्तव्यो रौक्ष्यकण्डूमलादिषु अरूंषिकाशिरस्तोददाहपाकव्रणेषु तु परिषेकः २४ पिचुः केशशातस्फुटनधूपने नेत्रस्तम्भे च बस्तिस्तु प्रसुप्त्यर्दितजागरे नासास्यशोषे तिमिरे शिरोरोगे च दारुणे २५-२६
transliteration: abhyaṅgasekapicavo bastiśceti caturvidham 23 mūrdhatailama bahuguṇaṃ tadvidyāt uttarottaram tatrābhyaṅgaḥ prayoktavyo raukṣyakaṇḍūmalādiṣu arūṃṣikāśirastodadāhapākavraṇeṣu tu pariṣekaḥ 24 picuḥ keśaśātasphuṭanadhūpane netrastambhe ca bastistu prasuppyarditajāgare nāsāsyaśoṣe timire śiroroge ca dāruṇe 25-26
commentary: Murdha Taila – application of oil to the head is of 4 types. Shiro Abhyanga – smearing oil and mild massage, Shiro Pariseka– pouring oil in continuous stream, Shiro Pichu – keeping cloth soaked in oil over the entire area of scalp, Shiro Basti – making the oil stand on the head with the help of a compound. Each successive one being more effective. Means, Shirobasti is the most effective among the four. Applying oil and doing mild massage should be used in cases of dryness, itching and dirtyness. Pouring oil in a thin stream is useful in ulcerations of the scalp, headache, burning sensation, wounds, and suppurations in the scalp. It is also known as Shirodhara. Oil soaked cloth / cotton swabs, applied over the scalp – useful in case of falling of hairs, cracking of the skin and feeling of burning sensation. Making the oil to stand on the head in cases of Netrasthamba – lack of movement of eyeball, Prasupti – loss of sensation of the scalp, Ardita – facial palsy, Jagara – loss of sleep, Nasa Asya Shosha – dryness of the nose and mouth, Timira – blindness and Daruna Shiroroga – dreadful diseases of the head.

sanskrit_text: विधिस्तस्य निषण्णस्य पीठे जानुसमे मृदौ शुद्धाभ्यक्तस्विन्नदेहस्य दिनान्ते गव्यमाहिषम् द्वादशाङ्गुलविस्तीर्णं चर्मपट्टं शिरः आकर्णबन्धनस्थानं ललाटे वस्त्रवेष्टिते चैलवेणिकया बद्ध्वा माषकल्केन लेपयेत् ततो यथाव्याधि श्रुतं स्नेहं कोष्णं निषेचयेत् ऊर्ध्वं केशभुवो यावदङ्गुलं धारयेच्च तम् आवक्त्रनासिकोक्लेदाद्दशाष्टौ षट् चलादिषु २७-३० मात्रासहस्राण्यरुजे त्वेकं स्कन्धादि मर्दयेत् मुक्तस्नेहस्य परमं सप्ताहं तस्य सेवनम् ३१ धारयेत्पूर्णं कर्णे कर्णमूलं विमर्दयन् रुजः स्यान्मार्दवं यावन्मात्राशतमवेदने ३२ यावत्पर्येति हस्ताग्रं दक्षिणं जानुमण्डलम् निमेषोन्मेषकालेन समं मात्रा तु सा स्मृता ३३
transliteration: vidhistasya niṣaṇṇasya pīṭhe jānusame mṛdau śuddhābhyaktasvinnadehasya dinānte gavyamāhiṣam dvādaśāṅgulavistīrṇaṃ carmapaṭṭaṃ śiraḥ ākarṇabandhanasthānaṃ lalāṭe vastraveṣṭite cailaveṇikayā baddhvā māṣakalkena lepayet tato yathāvyādhi śrutaṃ snehaṃ koṣṇaṃ niṣecayet ūrdhvaṃ keśabhuvō yāvadaṅgulaṃ dhārayecca tam āvaktranāsikokledādaśāṣṭau ṣaṭ calādiṣu 27-30 mātrāsahasrāṇyaruje tvekaṃ skandhādi mardayet mukt snehasya paramaṃ saptāhaṃ tasya sevanam 31 dhārayetpūrṇaṃ karṇe karṇamūlaṃ vimardayan ru jaḥ syānmārdavaṃ yāvanmātrāśatamavedane 32 yāvatparyeti hastāgraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalam nimeṣonmeṣakālena samaṃ mātrā tu sā smṛtā 33
commentary: The person who has been purified – with Vamana, Virechana etc., should be gently massaged with oil and given mild fomentation. Then at the closing of the day (evening) he should be made to sit on a stool of the height of the knee, a strap of leather made from the leather of either cow or buffalo, twelve Angula in width (8 – 9 inches) and equal to that of the head in circumference should be wrapped around the head, just above the ears, covered by a piece of cloth over the forehead, and fastened tight with a thread. The joints and intervening spaces should be packed with paste of black gram flour in order to prevent leakage of oil. Then, medicated oil prescribed for the disease, should be poured over the head, in luke warm condition, to a height of one Angula over the skin of the scalp. It should be held till secretion of fluid appears in the mouth and nose, or for a period of 10,000 Matra Kala for Vata, 8,000 Matra Kala for Pitta and 6,000 Matra Kala for Kapha. 1 Matra Kala = time required to blink the eye once. For a healthy person, it is 1,000 Matra Kala. After this period, the shoulders etc. should be massaged, after removing the oil over the head. Seven days shall be the maximum period for this therapy. The ears should be filled with medicated fat/oil, root of the ears massaged, till the pain or the disease subsides and for a period of one thousand Matra Kala in case of healthy persons. The time required for the finger of the right hand to move around the right knee once or the time required for closing and opening of the eyelids once is defined as a Matrakala.

sanskrit_text: कचसदनासिततवपिञ्जरत्वं परिफुटशिरसः समीररोगान् जयति जनयति इन्द्रियप्रसादं स्वरहनुमूर्ध्वबलं च मूर्धतैलम्
transliteration: kacasadanāsitatavapiñjaratvaṃ pariphuṭaśirasaḥ samīrarogān jayati janayati indriyaprasādaṃ svarahanumūrdhvabalaṃ ca mūrdhatailam
commentary: Oiling of the head prevents/cures falling, graying and matting of the hair, cracking of skin of the scalp, diseases of the head of Vata imbalance, produces clarity of sense organs, imparts strength to the voice, jaw and head.

topic_heading: Aschotana – Herbal eye drops and Vidhi
sanskrit_text: सर्वेष्वेवाक्षिरोगेषु हितमश्चोतनं सदा रुक्तोदकण्डूघर्षाश्रुदाहरागापहम् १ उष्णं वाते हितं कोष्णं कफे शीतं च रक्तपित्ते २ अथ स्यादश्चोतनविधिः निवातशयने पुमान् वामेनोन्मील्य नयनं दक्षिणेन शनैः शुचिः द्व्यङ्गुलोच्छ्रितया वर्त्या शुक्त्या वा किञ्चिदूर्ध्वतः दश द्वादश वा बिन्दून् पातयेदक्षि निर्भरम् ३ शनैरुन्मील्य पिचुना श्लक्ष्णेनाक्षि प्रमार्जयेत् कफवातोत्थिते रोगे स्वेदयेदुष्णवाससा रक्तपित्तोत्थिते शीतैः प्लोतैः संस्पर्शयेन्मुहुः ४ अतितप्तातिबिन्दुत्वाक्ष्णोः शूलरागतमःकृतः शीततीक्ष्णैस्तथात्यर्थतोदस्तब्धासुखावहः अतियोगात्खरस्पर्शशुक्त्वगुद्घाटनं भवेत् ५ अयोगाद्व्याधिकोपः स्यात्सशोफरुगरागवान् स्रावश्च स्नेहयुक्तेन स्निग्धेनाग्न्यातपादिना ६ मुखनासाक्षिसन्धीनां प्रविष्टं शिरसः सिराः शोधयत्यञ्जनं तस्मादुत्तमाङ्गगतान्मलान् ७
transliteration: sarveṣvevākṣirogeṣu hitamaścotanaṃ sadā ruktodakaṇḍūgharṣāśrudāharāgāpaham 1 uṣṇaṃ vāte hitaṃ koṣṇaṃ kaphe śītaṃ ca raktapitte 2 atha syādaścotanavidhiḥ nivātaśayane pumān vāmenonmīlya nayanaṃ dakṣiṇena śanaiḥ śuciḥ dvyāṅgulocchritayā vartyā śuktyā vā kiñcidūrdhvataḥ daśa dvādaśa vā bindūn pātayedakṣi nirbharam 3 śanairunmīlya picunā ślakṣṇenākṣi pramārjayet kaphavātotthite roge svedayeduṣṇavāsasā raktapittotthite śītaiḥ plotaiḥ saṃsparśayenmuhuḥ 4 atitaptātibindutvākṣṇoḥ śūlarāgatamaḥkṛtaḥ śītatīkṣṇaistathātyarthatodastabdhāsukhāvahaḥ atiyogātkharasparśaśuktvagudghāṭanaṃ bhavet 5 ayogādvyādhikopaḥ syātsaśopharugarāgavān srāvaśca snehayuktena snigdhenāgnyātapādinā 6 mukhanāsākṣisandhīnāṃ praviṣṭaṃ śirasaḥ sirāḥ śodhayatyañjanaṃ tasmāduttamāṅgagatānmalān 7
commentary: In all diseases of the eyes, Aschotana (eye drops) is very beneficial. It helps to prevent Ruk – eye pain, Toda – pricking pain, Kandu – eye itching, Gharsha – feeling of friction in the eyes, Ashru – excessive lacrimation, tears, Daha – burning sensation, Raga – eye redness. Drops of medicated liquids should be warm in case of Vata imbalance, lukewarm in Kapha imbalance and cold in Rakta (blood) and Pitta imbalance. The person should lie on a cot in a place devoid of breeze. His eyes should be opened with the left hand of the physician. The medicine dispenser, either a seashell or a wick is held in the right hand of the physician just two Angulas (finger width) above the inner angle of the eye (inner canthus). 10 – 12 drops of the medicated liquid are put into the eye. Afterwards the eyes should be cleaned with soft cloth. Mild fomentation is given with a piece of cloth rinsed in warm water in disorders of Kapha and Vata. In disorders due to blood and Pitta vitiation, eyes are mopped with a cloth dipped in cold water. Very hot and strong medicinal drops lead to pain, redness and loss of vision; Very cold drops produce pricking pain, loss of movement of eye balls and discomfort; Excess therapy produces roughness of the lids, friction and difficulty in opening of the lids; Inadequate (less) therapy leads to worsening of the diseases, increase of swelling, redness and absence of lacrimation. The medicine dropped into the eye, entering into the channels of the joints (fornices of the eyes), head, nose and face, eliminates the imbalanced Doshas which have localized in the upper parts of the body.

sanskrit_text: अथाञ्जनं शुद्धतनोर्नेत्रमात्राश्रये मले पक्वलिङ्गाल्पशोफातिकण्डुपैच्छिल्यलक्षिते ८ मन्दघर्षाश्रुरागे अक्ष्णः प्रयोज्यं घनदूषिके आर्ते पित्तकफास्रक्भिः मारुतेन विशेषतः ९ लेखनं रोपणं दृष्टिप्रसादनमिति त्रिधा अञ्जनं लेखनं तत्र कषायाम्लपटूषणैः रोपणं तिक्तकैर्द्रव्यैः स्वादुशीतैः प्रसादनम् १०-११ तीक्ष्णाञ्जनाभिसन्तप्ते नयने तत्प्रसादनं प्रयुज्यमानं लभते प्रत्यञ्जनसमाह्वयम् १२ दशाङ्गला तनुमध्ये शलाका मुकुलानना प्रशस्ता, लेखने ताम्री रोपणे काललोहजा अङ्गुली च सुवर्णोत्था रूप्यजा च प्रसादने १३
transliteration: athāñjanaṃ śuddhatanornetramātrāśraye male pakvaliṅgālpaśophātikaṇḍupaicchilyalakṣite 8 mandagharṣāśrurāge akṣṇaḥ prayojyaṃ ghanadūṣike ārte pittakaphāsrakbhiḥ mārutena viśeṣataḥ 9 lekhanaṃ ropaṇaṃ dṛṣṭiprasādanamiti tridhā añjanaṃ lekhanaṃ tatra kaṣāyāmlapaṭūṣaṇaiḥ ropaṇaṃ tiktakairdravyaiḥ svāduśītaiḥ prasādanam 10-11 tīkṣṇāñjanābhisantapte nayane tatprasādanaṃ prayujyamānaṃ labhate pratyañjanasamāhvayam 12 daśāṅgalā tanumadhye śalākā mukulānanā praśastā, lekhane tāmrī ropaṇe kālalohajā aṅgulī ca suvarṇotthā rūpyajā ca prasādane 13
commentary: Application of collyrium is suitable for the person who has his body purified by Vamana, Virechana etc, in whom the Doshas are localized in the eyes only, when signs of fully ripened state such as slight oedema (Alpa shopha), severe itching (Ati kandu) and sliminess (Paichilya) are found, when the excretions of the eyes are thick, in persons who are being troubled by Pitta, Kapha and blood and especially in Vata imbalance. Anjana is of three kinds – Lekhana – scarifying, scraping, Ropana – healing and Drishti prasadana – making the vision clear, soothing to the eyes; Lekhana Anjana is prepared from herbs of astringent, sour, salt, and pungent tastes and hot potency; Ropana Anjana is prepared from herbs of bitter taste and Prasadana Anjana from herbs of sweet taste and cold potency. To combat the side effects of strong collyrium, Prasadana Anjana is used. This kind of usage of one Anjana against the effects of the other is called as Pratyanjana – counter collyrium. A metal rod, 10 Angula in length, thin in the middle, with tips resembling a flower bud is best suited for Anjana application. For Lekhana Anjana, the Shalaka should be made of copper. For Ropana, it should be made of iron or finger itself can be used. For Prasadana, Shalaka of gold and silver is used.

sanskrit_text: पिण्डो रसक्रिया चूर्णस्त्रिधैवाञ्जनकल्पना गुरौ मध्ये लघौ दोषे तां क्रमेण प्रयोजयेत् १४ हरेणुमात्रा पिण्डस्य तीक्ष्णस्य, द्विगुणं तस्य मृदुनः वेल्लमात्रा रसक्रिया चूर्णितस्य च द्वे शालाके तु तीक्ष्णस्य, तिस्रस्तदितरस्य च १५ निशि स्वप्ने न मध्याह्ने म्लाने नोष्णगर्भास्तभिः १६ अक्षिरोगयदोषाः स्युर्वृद्धितोपद्रुताः प्रातः सायं च तच्छान्त्यै व्यभ्रेअर्क अतो अञ्जयेत्सदा १७ वदन्त्यन्ये तु न दिवा प्रयोज्यं तीक्ष्णमनञ्जनम् विरेकदुर्बलं चक्षुरादित्यं प्राप्य सीदति १८ स्वप्नेन रात्रौ कालस्य सौम्यत्वेन च तर्पिता शीतसात्म्यादग्नेयी स्थिरतां लभते पुनः १९ अत्युद्रिक्ते बलासे तु लेखनीये अथवा गदे काममह्न्यपि नात्युष्णे तीक्ष्णमक्ष्णि प्रयोजयेत् २० अश्मनो जन्म लोहस्य तत एव च तीक्ष्णता उपगतोऽपि तेनैव तथा नेत्रस्य तेजसः २१ न रात्रावपि शीतेऽति नेत्रे तीक्ष्णाञ्जनं हितम् दोषमस्रावयेत्स्तब्धं कण्डूजाड्यादिकारि तत् २२
transliteration: piṇḍo rasakriyā cūrṇastridhaivāñjanakalpanā gurau madhye laghau doṣe tāṃ krameṇa prayojayet 14 hareṇumātrā piṇḍasya tīkṣṇasya, dviguṇaṃ tasya mṛdunaḥ vellamātrā rasakriyā cūrṇitasya ca dve śālāke tu tīkṣṇasya, tisrastaditarasya ca 15 niśi svapne na madhyāhne mlāne noṣṇagarbhāstabhiḥ 16 akṣirogayadoṣāḥ syurvṛddhitopadrutāḥ prātaḥ sāyaṃ ca tacchāntyai vyabhrearka ato añjayetsadā 17 vadantyanye tu na divā prayojyaṃ tīkṣṇamanañjanam virekadurbalaṃ cakṣurādityaṃ prāpya sīdati 18 svapnena rātrau kālasya saumyatvena ca tarpitā śītasātmyād agneyī sthiratāṃ labhate punaḥ 19 atyudrikte balāse tu lekhaniye athavā gade kāmamahnyapi nātyuṣṇe tīkṣṇamakṣṇi prayojayet 20 aśmano janma lohasya tata eva ca tīkṣṇatā upagato'pi tenaiva tathā netrasya tejasaḥ 21 na rātrāvapi śīte'ti netre tīkṣṇāñjanaṃ hitam doṣamasrāvayetstab dhaṃ kaṇḍūjāḍyādikāri tat 22
commentary: Pinda – pill – used in profound imbalance of Dosha, Rasakriya – gel, confection, semisolid got from boiling decoction till solidity - used in moderate imbalance of Dosha, Churna – powder are the three forms of Anjana – used in mild imbalance of Dosha. The quantity of Pinda anjana prepared from strong herbs is one Harenu. The quantity of Pinda Collyrium prepared from mild herbs is two Harenu. The quantity of eye-salve which is in the form of gel, confection (Rasakriya) shall be that of Vella (Vidanga), the quantity of the eye salve which is in the form of powder (Churna) is two rods full in case of strong herbs and three rods full in case of mild herbs. Application of eye-salve (collyrium) should NOT be made at nights, during sleep, at midday, when the eyes are fatigued by strong rays of the sun. If done during these times, it will lead to diseases of the eyes because the Doshas get increased, spread to other sites and get liquefied. So to mitigate the Doshas, Anjana should be applied always either in the morning or in the evening when the sun is not present. Others say, that strong Anjana should not be applied during day, because the eye which has become weak by purgation treatment from strong herbs will be further debilitated by the presence of the sun. The eye is Agneyi – predominant with the fire element, being habituated to cold comforts it regains its strength after good sleep and nourished by the coolant nature of the night. In condition of extreme increase of Kapha or in diseases which require Lekhana Anjana – scraping type, Teekshna Anjana – strong type, can be put into the eyes even during day time, if desired, only if the day is not very hot. Metals are born from the ores; From ores only they – metals derive their sharpness / bluntness. Similarly, the eyes derive their power and features by Agni – Fire element. When there is severe cold, application of strong eye-salve is not good even at nights, because it does not cause elimination of the Doshas from the eyes. Instead, it produces itching, inactivity etc. Here Doshas get stagnated inside the eyes, even after Anjana therapy, due to cold effect.

sanskrit_text: नाञ्जनेद्भीतवमितविरिक्ताशितवेगिते क्रुद्धज्वरितताप्ताक्षिशिरोरुक्शोकजागरे अदृष्टेअर्के शिरः स्नाते पीतयोर्धूममद्ययोः अजीर्णेअग्न्यर्कसन्तप्ते दिवासुप्ते पिपासिते २३-२४ अतितीक्ष्णमृदुस्तोकबहुश्लघनकर्कशम् । अत्यर्थशीतलं तप्तमञ्जनं नावचारयेत् २५ अथानुमीलयन् दृष्टिमन्तः सञ्चारयेच्छनैः अञ्जिते वर्त्मनी तीक्ष्णं व्याप्नोति सहसा, न चोन्मेषनिमेषणम् निष्पीडनं च वर्त्मभ्यां क्षालनं वा समाचरेत् २६-२७ अपेतौषधसंरम्भं निर्वृतं नयनं यदा व्याधिदोषर्तुयोग्याभिरद्भिः प्रक्षालयेत्तदा २८ दक्षिणाङ्गुष्ठकेनाक्षि ततो वामं सवाससा उद्धृत्य वर्त्मनि सङ्गृह्य शोध्यं वामेन चेतरत् २९ वर्त्मप्राप्तो अञ्जाद्दोषो रोगान् कुर्यादतोऽन्यथा कण्डूजाड्येअञ्जनं तीक्ष्णं धूमं वा योजयेत् पुनः ३०
transliteration: nāñjaned bhītavamitaviriktāśitavegite kruddhajvaritatāptākṣiśirorukśokajāgare adṛṣṭe arke śiraḥ snāte pītayordhūmamadyayoḥ ajīrṇe agnyarkasantapte divāsupte pipāsite 23-24 atitīkṣṇamṛdustokabahuślaghanakarkaśam | atyarthaśītalaṃ taptamañjanaṃ nāvacārayet 25 athānumīlayan dṛṣṭimantaḥ sañcārayecchanaiḥ añjite vartmanī tīkṣṇaṃ vyāpnoti sahasā, na conmeṣanimeṣaṇam niṣpīḍanaṃ ca vartmabhyāṃ kṣālanaṃ vā samācaret 26-27 apetauṣadhasaṃrambhaṃ nirvṛtaṃ nayanaṃ yadā vyādhid oṣartuyogyābhiradbhiḥ prakṣālayettadā 28 dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhakenākṣi tato vāmaṃ savāsasā uddhṛtya vartmani saṅgṛhya śodhyaṃ vāmena cetarat 29 vartmaprāpto añjādddoṣo rogān kuryādato'nyathā kaṇḍūjāḍye añjanaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ dhūmaṃ vā yojayet punaḥ 30
commentary: Application of Anjana should not be done to persons who are Bheeta – in fear, Vamita, Virikta – who have been administered Vamana and Virechana, who are hungry, Shitavegita – who have urges of urine, faeces etc., Kruddha – anger; Jvarita – during fever, when the eyes are fatigued, Shiroruk – during headache, Shoka – bouts of grief and Jagara – loss of sleep; Adurshte Arke – when the sun is fully covered with clouds, Shira Snate – after head bath, after inhalation of smoke and drinking of wine, Ajirne – during indigestion, fatigued from excess exposure to fire and sun; Divasupte – soon after sleep during day and Pipasite – when thirsty. Anjana, which is very strong or very mild, very little or very large in quantity, very thin or very thick in consistency, very rough, coarse, very cold or very hot – should not be used. After applying the Anjana, the eye balls should be moved up and rotated slowly, the eyelids should also be moved slight by massaging over it; by these acts the strong eye salve spreads to all places. But opening and closing, squeezing or washing of the eyelids should not be done. After the cessation of the activity of the drug, when the eyes have regained strength, they should be washed with water – hot or cold, suitable to the disease, Doshas and season. The physician should lift and hold the upper lid of the left eye with a piece of cloth held in his right thumb and fingers and wash the left eye; with his left hand, the other eye. Otherwise, if not washed the Anjana remaining in the lids, excites the Doshas which give rise to diseases. In case of itching and inactivity either a strong Anjana should be applied again or an inhalation of strong smoke of herbs should be done. When the eyes are fatigued by strong Anjana, applying a Pratyanjana – counter eye-salve which is in the form of powder and cold in effect should be done.

sanskrit_text: नयने ताम्यति स्तब्धे शुष्के रुक्षे अभिघातिते वातपित्तातुरे जिह्मे शीर्णपक्ष्माविलक्षणे १ कृच्छ्रोन्मीलशिराहर्षशिरोत्पाततमोऽर्जुनैः स्यन्दमन्थान्यतोवातपर्यायशुक्रकैः २ आतुरे शान्तरागाश्रुशूलसंरम्भदूषिके ३ निवाते तर्पणं योज्यं शुद्धयोर्मूर्धकाययोः काले साधारणे प्रातः सायं वोत्तानशायिनः ४ यवमाषमयीं पालीं नेत्रकोशात् बहिः समाम् द्वयङ्गुलोच्चां दृढां कृत्वा यथास्वं सिद्धमावपेत सर्पिर्निमील्यते नेत्रे तप्ताम्बुप्रविलायितम् ५ नक्तान्ध्यवाततिमिरकृच्छ्रबोधादिके वसाम् अपक्ष्माग्रात् अथोन्मेषं शनकैस्तस्य कुर्वतः ६ मात्रा विगणयेत्तत्र वर्त्मसन्धिसितासिते दृष्टौ च क्रमशो व्याधौ शतं त्रीणि च पञ्च च शतानि सप्त चाष्टौ च , दश मन्थे , दशानिले पित्ते षट्, स्वस्थवृत्ते च वलासे पञ्च चारयेत् ७-९ कृत्वापाङ्गे ततो द्वारं स्नेहं पात्रे निगोलयेत् पिबेच्च धूमं, नेक्षेत व्योम रूपं च भास्वरम् १० इत्थं प्रतिदिनं वायौ, पित्ते त्वेकान्तरं, कफे स्वस्थे च द्व्यन्तरं दद्यादातृप्तिरेति योजयेत् ११
transliteration: nayane tāmyati stabdhe śuṣke rūkṣe abhighātite vātapittāture jihme śīrṇapakṣmāvilakṣaṇe 1 kṛcchronmīlaśirāharṣaśirotpātatamo'rjunaiḥ syandamanthānyatovātaparyāyaśukrakaiḥ 2 āture śāntarāgāśruśūlasaṃrambhadūṣike 3 nivāte tarpaṇaṃ yojyaṃ śuddhayormūrdhakāyayoḥ kāle sādhāraṇe prātaḥ sāyaṃ vottānaśāyinaḥ 4 yavamāṣamayīṃ pālīṃ netrakośāt bahiḥ samām dvayaṅguloccāṃ dṛḍhāṃ kṛtvā yathāsvaṃ siddhamāvapet sarpirnimīlyate netre taptāmbupravilāyitam 5 naktāndhyavātatimirakṛcchrabodhādike vasām apakṣmāgrāt athonmeṣaṃ śanakaistasya kurvataḥ 6 mātrā vigaṇayettatra vartmasandhitasite dṛṣṭau ca kramaśo vyādhau śataṃ trīṇi ca pañca ca śatāni sapta cāṣṭau ca, daśa manthe, daśānile pitte ṣaṭ, svasthavṛtte ca valāse pañca cārayet 7-9 kṛtvāpāṅge tato dvāraṃ snehaṃ pātre nigolayet pibec ca dhūmaṃ, nekṣeta vyoma rūpaṃ ca bhāsvaram 10 itthaṃ pratidinaṃ vāyau, pitte tvekāntaraṃ, kaphe svastha ca dvyantaraṃ dadyādātṛptireti yojayet 11
commentary: Indications for Tarpana eye care procedure: When the eyes are fatigued, stiff, dry, rough or injured; in patients of increase of Vata and Pitta; when there is irregularity – Asymmetry or loss of eye Lashes, in clouded unclear vision; in patients of – diseases like Krchronmilla –difficulty in opening eyes, Shiraharsha, Shirotpata – redness and hemorrhage, Tama – darkness in front of eyes, Arjuna, Syanda, Mantha, Anyato Vata, Vataparyaya, and Sukraka; After relief from redness lacrimation, pain, swelling and exertions. The patient should undergo purification of head – Nasya treatment and also purification of body – Vamana and Virechana. Time for Tarpana can be either morning or evening. The patient is lying with his face upwards in a room devoid of breeze. A wall is constructed with the paste prepared from Yava (barley) and Masha (black gram) around eye socket –resembling a well to a height of two Angula –finger breadth. Keeping the eyelids closed, medicated herbal ghee, which is liquefied by heating in hot water bed, should be poured into the well up to the level of tips of the eye lashes. In diseases like Naktandhya (night blindness), Vatatimira, Krichradodha etc. muscle fat should be used instead of ghee. The patient should then be asked to open his eyes slowly and retain the drug. Time required to utter a soft syllable should be counted up to 100 – for the diseases of Vartma – eye lids, 300 – for the diseases of Sandhi – fornices, 500 – for the diseases of Sita – sclera, 700 – for the diseases of Asita – cornea, 800 – for the diseases of Drishti – pupil, retina etc., 1000 – for the disease Adhimanta, 1000 – for the disease caused by Vata imbalance, 600 – for diseases caused by Pitta, 500 – for healthy person and for diseases of Kapha imbalance. These are the time for retaining the drug. After the stipulated time, the ghee should be removed through a hole done at the outer canthus. The person should be given Dhumapana (herbal smoking). The person is advised not to look at the bright sky or bright objects. Tarpana therapy should be done daily in diseases of Vata, On alternative days in diseases of Pitta, with an interval of two days for the healthy persons and in diseases of kapha. Prakasha Kshamata – Ability to withstand bright light, Good eye health, Vishada – clarity in vision, Laghu lochana – lightness in eyes are the symptoms of good Tarpana procedure. Opposite of these are the symptoms of inadequate Tarpana and appearance of disorders of Kapha imbalance is the symptom of Excess Tarpana.

sanskrit_text: तर्पणं पुटपाकं च नस्यानर्हे न योजयेत् यावन्त्यहानि युञ्जीत द्विस्ततो हितमांभवेत् मालतीमल्लिकापुष्पैर्बद्धाक्षो निबसेन्निशाम् १२ स्नेहपीता तनुरिव क्लान्ता दृष्टिर्हि सीदति तर्पणानन्तरं तस्मात् दृक् बलाधानकारिणम् १२ पुटपाकं प्रयुञ्जीत पूर्वोक्तेष्वेव यक्ष्मसु १३ स वाते स्नेहनः, श्लेष्मसहिते लेखनो हितः दृग्दौर्बल्यानिले पित्तेरक्ते स्वस्थे प्रसादनः १४ भूशयप्रसहानूपमेदोमज्जवसामिषैः स्नेहनं पयसा पिष्टैःजीवनीयैश्च कल्पयेत् १५ मृगपक्षियकृन्मांसमुक्तायस्ताम्रसैन्धवैः स्रोतोजराशङ्खफेनालैर्लेखनं मस्तुकल्कितैः १६ मृगपक्षियकृन्मज्जवसास्थिहृदयामिषैः मधुरैःसघृतैः स्तन्यक्षीरपिष्टैः प्रसादनम् १७ बिल्वमात्रं पृथक् पिण्डं मांसं भेषजकल्कयोः १७ उरुबूकवटाम्भोजपत्रैः स्नेहादिषु क्रमात् वेष्टयित्वा मृदा लिप्तं धवधन्वनगोमयैः १८ पचेत्प्रदीप्तैः अग्न्याभं पक्वं निष्पीड्य तद्रसम् नेत्रे तर्पणवत् युञ्ज्यात् शतं द्वे त्रीणि धारयेत् लेखनस्नेहनान्त्येषु कोष्णौ पूर्वौ, हिम अपरः धूमपः अन्ते तयोरेव १९ योगास्त्वत्र च तृप्तिवत् २० तर्पणं पुटपाकं च नस्यानर्हे न योजयेत् यावन्त्यहानि युञ्जीत द्विस्ततो हितमांभवेत् मालतीमल्लिकापुष्पैर्बद्धाक्षो निबसेन्निशाम् २१ सर्वात्मनां नेत्रबलाय यत्नं कुर्वीत नस्याञ्जनतर्पणाद्यैः दृष्टिश्च नष्टा विविधं जगच्च तमोमयं जायत एकरूपम् २२
transliteration: tarpaṇaṃ puṭapākaṃ ca nasyānarhe na yojayet yāvantyahāni yuñjīta dvistato hitamāṃbhavet mālatīmallikāpuṣpairbaddhākṣo nibasennishām 12 snehapītā tanuriva klāntā dṛṣṭirhi sīdati tarpaṇānantaraṃ tasmāt dṛk balādhānakāriṇam 12 puṭapākaṃ prayuñjīta pūrvokteṣveva yakṣmasu 13 sa vāte snehanaḥ, śleṣmasahite lekhano hitaḥ dṛgdaurbalyānile pitterakte svastha prasādanaḥ 14 bhūśayaprasahānūpamedomajjavasāmiṣaiḥ snehanaṃ payasā piṣṭaiḥ jīvanīyaiśca kalpayet 15 mṛgapakṣiyakṛnmāṃsamuktāyastāmrasaindhavaiḥ srotojarāśaṅkhaphenālair lekhanaṃ mastukalkitaiḥ 16 mṛgapakṣiyakṛnmajjavasāsthidayāmiṣaiḥ madhuraih saghṛtaiḥ stanyakṣīrapiṣṭaiḥ prasādanam 17 bilvamātraṃ pṛthak piṇḍaṃ māṃsaṃ bheṣajakalkayoḥ 17 urubūkavaṭāmbhojapatraiḥ snehādiṣu kramāt veṣṭayitvā mṛdā liptaṃ dhavadhanvanagomayaiḥ 18 pacetpradīptaiḥ agnyābaṃ pakvaṃ niṣpīḍya tadrasam netre tarpaṇavat yuñjyāt śataṃ dve trīṇi dhārayet lekhana snehanāntyeṣu koṣṇau pūrvau, hima aparaḥ dhūmapaḥ ante tayoreva 19 yogāstva tra ca tṛptivat 20 tarpaṇaṃ puṭapākaṃ ca nasyānarhe na yojayet yāvantyahāni yuñjīta dvistato hitamāṃbhavet mālatīmallikāpuṣpairbaddhākṣo nibasennishām 21 sarvātmanāṃ netrabalāya yatnaṃ kurvīta nasyāñjanatarpaṇādyaiḥ dṛṣṭiśca naṣṭā vividhaṃ jagacca tamomayaṃ jāyata ekārūpam 22
commentary: Both Tarpana and Putapaka therapies should not be administered to those who are unfit for Nasya. Those who have undergone tarpana and putapaka should adhere to - healthy foods and activities for double the number of days of these therapies; during nights, he should bind the eyes with a pad of flowers like malati, mallika etc. Just as the body becomes fatigued after Snehana therapy (drinking fats), eyes become fatigued after Tarpana therapy; In order to restore the strength to the eyes, Putapaka therapy should be done in diseases mentioned earlier. Snehana putapaka (with fat) – for Vata imbalance disorder. Lekhana Putapaka (scraping type) – for Vata – Kapha imbalance disorder. Prasadana Putapaka (soothing) – in weakness of the eyes, vision, in disorders of Vata Pitta and Rakta and for the healthy person. Snehana Putapaka is done by making use of fat, marrow, muscle fat and juice of meat of animals which live in burrows (Bhushaya), which bite (Prasaha) – cut their food, cow, horse, ass etc, and those which live in Marshy lands (Anupa), or with drugs of Jivaneeya gana- (chapter 15) macerated with milk. Lekhana Putapaka is by making use of Mastu (whey), water of yoghurt macerated with the paste of liver of animal and birds, pearls, ash of iron and copper, Saindhava- salt, Srotonjana (Antimony sulphide), Shankha (ash of conch shell), Phena- (sea foam), cuttlefish and Ala (orpiment ). Prasadana Putapaka is by the use of cow milk / breast milk macerated with the liver, marrow, Muscle fat, Muscle of intestines and heart of animals and birds and drugs of sweet taste, and mixed with ghee. The meat of animals and drugs should be made into balls of size of Bael fruit or of 1 pala (48 grams). The balls should be wrapped in leaves of Urubuka, Vata or Amboja, Smeared with fats, and given a coating of mud. After they become dry, they are placed inside the fire, of wood of Dhava or Dhavana or of dried crow dung and cooked till the balls become fire like red in appearance. After they cool off, the paste of drugs is taken out and juice extracted from it. The juice should be used for Tarpana procedure, as explained above. The juice should be retained for a period of 200 – 300 Matra Kala. 200 for Snehana and Lekhana. 300 for Prasadhana. Juice should be Lukewarm for the Snehana and Lekhana and cold for Prasadana. At the end of the Snehana and Lekhana types, Dhumpana (medicated smoking) is indicated. The signs and symptoms of proper, inadequate or excess of Putapaka therapy are similar to those mentioned under Tarpana therapy. The patient who has undergone Tarpana and Putapaka therapies should adhere to healthy foods and activities for double the number of days of Nasya therapy. During nights he should bind the eyes with a pad of flowers like Malati, Mallika (Jasmine varieties). All out efforts should be made to strengthen the eyes by following Nasya, Anjana, Tarpana etc, for once the vision is lost the different types of things of the world will all become one types of thing – darkness.

sanskrit_text: नानाविधानं शल्यानां नानादेशप्रबाधिनाम् आहर्तुमुपायो यस्तत् यन्त्रं यच्च दर्शने १ अर्शोभगन्दरादीनां शस्त्रक्षाराग्नियोजने शेषाङ्गपरिरक्षायां तथा बस्त्यादिकर्मणि- २ घटिकालाबुशृङ्गं च जाम्बवौष्टादिकानि
transliteration: nānāvidhānaṃ śalyānāṃ nānādeśaprabādhinām āhartumupāyo yastat yantraṃ yacca darśane 1 arśobhagandarādīnāṃ śastrakṣārāgniyojane śeṣāṅgaparirakṣāyāṃ tathā bastryādikarmaṇi- 2 ghaṭikālābuśṛṅgaṃ ca jāmbavauṣṭādikāni
commentary: Equipments which are useful to extract the different types of foreign bodies causing pain in different parts of the body, to look into hemorrhoids, rectal fistula etc., to apply sharp instruments, Alkalies (Kshara) and fire (Agni Karma); to protect the remaining parts other than the diseased in therapies like enema etc, and the pot (Ghatika), ground horn (Alabu) of animal, Jambavaustha- cylindrical smooth stone etc. are all known as yantra (medical instruments). Yantras (instruments) are of many shapes, functions, types, hence they are to be fabricated and to be prepared with intelligence.

topic_heading: Swastika, Samdamsha, Muchundi and Tala Yantra
sanskrit_text: विकल्प्य कल्पयेद्बुद्ध्या यथास्थूलं तु वक्ष्यते तुल्यानि कङ्कसिंहर्क्षकाकादिमृगपक्षिणाम् मुखैर्मुखानि यन्त्राणां कुर्यात तत्संज्ञकानि च ३ अष्टादशाङ्गुलायामान्यायसानि च भूरिशः मसूराकार-पर्यन्तैः कण्ठे बद्धानि कीलकैः विद्यात्स्वस्तिकत्रयाणि मूले अङ्कुशनतानि च तैर्दृढैरस्थिसंलग्नशल्याहरणमिष्यते ४-६ कीलकद्वयविमुक्ताग्रौ सन्दंषौ षोडश अङ्गुलौ त्वक्शिरास्नायुपिशितलग्नशल्यापकर्षणौ षडङ्गुलोऽन्यो हरणे सूक्ष्मशल्योपपक्ष्मणाम् ७-८ मुचुण्डी सूक्ष्मदन्ता र्जुर्मूले रुचकभूषणा गम्भीरव्रणमांसानाम् अर्मणःशोषितस्य च ९ द्वे दशाङ्गुले मत्स्यतालवत् द्वयेकतालके तालयन्त्रे स्मृते कर्णनाडीशल्यापहारिणी १०
transliteration: vikalpya kalpayedbuddhyā yathāsthūlaṃ tu vakṣyate tulyāni kaṅkasiṃharkṣakākādimṛgapakṣiṇām mukhairmukhāni yantrāṇāṃ kuryāta tatsaṃjñakāni ca 3 aṣṭādaśāṅgulāyāmānyāyasāni ca bhūriśaḥ masūrākāra-paryantaiḥ kaṇṭhe baddhāni kīlakaiḥ vidyātsvastikatrayāṇi mūle aṅkuśanatāni ca tairdṛḍhairasthisaṃlagn aśalyāharaṇamiṣyate 4-6 kīlakadvayavimuktāgrau sandamṣau ṣoḍaśa aṅgulau tvakśirāsnāyupiśitalagn aśalyāpakarṣaṇau ṣaḍaṅgulo'nyo haraṇe sūkṣmaśalyopapakṣmaṇām 7-8 mucuṇḍī sūkṣmadantā rjur mūle rucakabhūṣaṇā gambhīravraṇamāṃsānām armaṇaḥśoṣitasya ca 9 dve daśāṅgule matsyatālavat dvayekatālake tālayantre smṛte karṇanāḍīśalyāpahāriṇī 10
commentary: Yantras are described in brief, as follows; Those which have their mouth resembling the mouth of Kanka (heron), Simha (lion), Ruksha (bear), Kaka (crow) and other animals and birds should be prepared under the respective names of animals and birds. Swastika Yantras should be generally 18 Angula- fingers breadth –in length, They are made chiefly from iron; They are shaped like a Masura dala (cotyledon of a lentil) at its edges, held by a rivet bolt at their neck, slightly bent like an Ankusha (goad of the elephant) at its handle are known as Swastika yantra- Cruci from instruments. These are useful to pull out foreign bodies stuck hard in the bones. Samdamsha yantra – forceps are of two types – one with a catch at its tip and the other without a catch. The one with a catch is 16 Angula length, used for extracting foreign bodies stuck up in the skin, veins, tendons and muscles.; The one without a catch is 6 Angula in length and useful for extracting small foreign bodies and eye lashes. Muchundi Yantra – forceps with teeth has small teeth, straight, with tooth catch, hook at its root; useful for pulling out the fleshy parts from deep wounds and remnants of flesh from the Arma (pterygium), which has been cut. Talayantra- instruments with flat arms are of two types- 12 Angula length, resembling the palate (fin) of the fish in shape, - with one flat disc at its mouth; - with two flat disc; Both are useful for removing foreign bodies from the orifice of the ear.

sanskrit_text: नाडीयन्त्राणि सुषिराणि एकानेकमुखानि च स्रोतोगतानां शल्यानां आमयानां च दर्शने क्रियाणां सुकरत्वाय कुर्यात् आचूषणाय च तद्विस्तारपरिणाहदैर्घ्यं स्रोतोनुरोधतः ११-१२ दशाङ्गुला अर्धनाहा अन्तः कण्ठशल्यावलोकिनी नाडी पञ्चमुखच्छिद्रा चतुष्कर्णस्य सङ्ग्रहे वारङ्गस्य, द्विकर्णस्य त्रिच्छिद्रा तत्प्रमाणतः वारङ्गकर्णसंस्थानानाहदैर्घ्यानुरोधतः नाडीरेवंविधाश्चान्या दृष्टं शल्यानि कारयेत् १३-१४ पद्मकर्णिकया मूर्ध्नि सदृशी द्वादशाङ्गुला चतुर्थसुषिरा नाडी शल्यनिर्घातिनी मता
transliteration: nāḍīyantrāṇi suṣirāṇi ekānekamukhāni ca srotogatānāṃ śalyānāṃ āmayānāṃ ca darśane kriyāṇāṃ sukaratvāya kuryāt ācūṣaṇāya ca tadvis tāra pariṇāhadairghyaṃ srotonurodhataḥ 11-12 daśāṅgulā ardhanāhā antaḥ kaṇṭhaśalyāvalokinī nāḍī pañcamukhacchidrā catuṣkarṇasya saṅgrahe vāraṅgasya, dvikarṇasya tricchidrā tatpramāṇataḥ vāraṅgakarṇasaṃsthānānāhadairghyānurodhataḥ nāḍīrevaṃvidhāścānyā dṛṣṭaṃ śalyāni kārayet 13-14 padmakarṇikayā mūrdhni sadṛśī dvādaśāṅgulā caturthasuṣirā nāḍī śalyanirghātinī matā
commentary: Nadiyantra - Tubular instruments (probe) are hollow, with one or more opening, useful for looking into body parts, recognizing foreign bodies and diseases localized in the channels of the tissues, for facilitating treatments and for sucking out. Their width, perimeter vary as per size, shape etc. of the channels. Nadi Yantra for seeing inside throat shall be 10 Angula in length and ½ Angula in thickness diameter. Nadi Yantra comes with many openings (4 – 5) with different size, length, thickness etc. Many other tubular instruments may be prepared to observe the foreign bodies, depending on the shape, thickness and length of the part to be observed. The tubular instrument having the shape of Padma Karnika – the round, flat central part of the lotus studded with small holes- at its top, twelve Angula – finger breath in length, with a hollow area of one fourth – it length is useful for catching and removing the foreign body.

topic_heading: Arsho Yantra, Samiyantra, Anguli Tranaka and others
sanskrit_text: अर्शसां गोस्तनाकारं यन्त्रकं चतुरङ्गुलम् नाहे पञ्चाङ्गुलं पुंसां प्रमदानां षडङ्गुलम् द्विच्छिद्रं दर्शने व्याधेरेकच्छिद्रं तु कर्मणि मध्येअस्य त्र्यङ्गुलं छिद्रमङ्गुष्टोदरविस्तृतम् अर्धाङ्गुलोच्छ्रतोद्वृत्तकर्णिकं च तदूर्ध्वतः १६-१८ शम्याख्यं तादृगच्छिद्रं यन्त्रमर्शः प्रपीडनम् १९ सर्वथा अपनयेदोष्ठं छिद्रादूर्ध्वं भगन्दरे घ्राणार्बुदार्शसामेकच्छिद्रा नाङ्ग्यङ्गुलद्वया प्रदेशिनीपरीणाहा स्याद्भगन्दरयन्त्रवत् २० अङ्गुलित्राणकं दान्तं वार्क्षं वा चतुरङ्गुलम् द्विच्छिद्रं गोस्तनाकारं तद्वक्त्रविवृतौ सुखम् २१ योनिव्रणेक्षणं मध्ये सुषिरं षोडशाङ्गुलम् मुद्राबद्धं चतुर्भित्तमम्भोजमुकुलाननम् चतुः शलाकामाक्रान्तं मूले तद्विकसेन्मुखे २२ यन्त्रे नाडीव्रणाभ्यङ्गक्षालनाय षडङ्गुले बस्तियन्त्राकृती मूले मुखे अङ्गुष्ठकलायखे अग्रतो अकर्णिके मूले निबद्धमृदुचर्मणी २३-२४
transliteration: arśasāṃ gostanākāraṃ yantrakaṃ caturaṅgulam nāhe pañcāṅgulaṃ puṃsāṃ pramadānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgulam dvichidraṃ darśane vyādherekacchidraṃ tu karmaṇi madhyeasya tryaṅgulaṃ chidramaṅguṣṭodaravistṛtam ardhaṅgulocchratodvṛ ttakarṇikaṃ ca tadūrdhvataḥ 16-18 śamyākhyaṃ tādṛgacchidraṃ yantramarśaḥ prapīḍanam 19 sarvathā apanayedodṭhaṃ chidrādūrdhvaṃ bhagandare ghrāṇārbudārśasāmekacchidrā nāṅgyaṅguladvayā pradeśinīparīṇāhā syādbhagandarayantravat 20 aṅgulitrāṇakaṃ dāntaṃ vārkṣaṃ vā caturaṅgulam dvichidraṃ gostanākāraṃ tadvaktravivṛtau sukham 21 yonivraṇekṣaṇaṃ madhye suṣiraṃ ṣoḍaśāṅgulam mudrābaddhaṃ caturbhittamambhojamukulānanam catuḥ śalākamākrāntaṃ mūle tadvikasenmukhe 22 yantre nāḍīvraṇābhyaṅgakṣālanāya ṣaḍaṅgule bastiyantrākṛtī mūle mukhe aṅguṣṭhakalāyakhe agrato akarṇike mūle nibaddhamṛducarmaṇī 23-24
commentary: The Arsho Yantra- the instrument to view the hemorrhoid inside the rectum. It has cylindrical shape. Its circumference is 5 Angula in men and 6 Angula for women; with two orifices- one at each end, useful for seeing the pile masses and with one slit shall be at its centre three Angula in length and of the size of the middle portion of the thumb in widths, about half Angula above the slit three shall be a karnuka – edge, (rim). The instrument known as Samiyantra is similar- to the above but without the offices and useful for squeezing the pile masses. The Nadiyantra to see the malignant tumor and piles, polyp of the nose shall be with one orifice, two Angula in length, of the size of the index finger in thickness and resembling the instrument meant for rectal fistula. Anguli Tranaka- finger protector – is made from ivory / wood, 4 Angula in length, with 2 orifices- one at each end; shaped like the nipple of the cow and suitable to extend the finger (when in use). The instrument to look into the vagina and wounds shall be hollow in the middle, 16 Angula in length, with four flaps held tight by a ring, resembling the bud of a lotus in shape, fixed with four rods at its root – handling place and its mouth- opening like of the bud. Two instrument- one for oiling the sinus ulcer and the other for washing it shall be 6 Angula in length, having the shape of a Bastiyantra (enema nozzle) with an orifice at its root allowing the entry of the thumb and the orifice at its tip allowing round pea; without any edge, Rim at its tip and fixed with soft leather bag at its root.

topic_heading: Shringa, Alabu, Shalaka, Shanku and other Yantras
sanskrit_text: द्विद्वारा नलिका पिच्छनलिका वोदकोदरे धूमबस्त्यादियन्त्राणि निर्दिष्टानि यथायथम् २५ त्र्यङ्गुलास्यं भवेच्छृङ्गं चूषणे अष्टादशाङ्गुलम् अग्रं सिद्धार्थकच्छिद्रं सुन्दरं चुचुकाकृति २६ अलाबु द्वादशाङ्गुलं व्यासे षोडशाङ्गुलम् चतुरङ्गुलवृत्तास्यं सवर्ति रक्तकफापहम् २७ तद्वद्घटी हिता गुल्मविलयोन्नमने च सा २८ शलाकाख्यानि यन्त्राणि नानाकर्माकृतीनि च यथायोगप्रमाणानि तेषामेषणकर्मणि २९ उभे गण्डूपदमुखे स्रोतोभ्यः शल्यहारिणी मसूरदलवक्त्रे द्वे स्यात्तामष्टनवाङ्गुले ३० शङ्कवः षट् उभौ तेषां षोडशद्वादशाङ्गुलौ व्यूहने अहिफणावक्त्रौ द्वौ दशद्वादशाङ्गुलौ चालने शरपुङ्खास्यौ आहार्ये बडिशाकृती ३१ नतो अग्रे शङ्कुना तुल्यो गर्भशङ्कुरिति स्मृतः अष्टाङ्गुलायतस्तेन मूढगर्भं हरेत्स्त्रियाः ३२ अश्मर्यहरणं सर्पफणाबद्धकमग्रतः शरपुङ्खमुखं दन्तपातनं चतुरङ्गुलम् ३३ कार्पासविहितोष्णीषाः शालाकाः षट् प्रमार्जने पायावासन्नदूरार्थे द्वे दशद्वादशाङ्गुले ३४ द्वे षट्सप्ताङ्गुले घ्राणे, द्वे कर्णे अष्टनवाङ्गुले कर्णशोधनमश्वत्थपत्रप्रान्तं स्रुवाननम् ३५ शलाकाजाम्बवौष्ठानां क्षारे अग्नौ च पृथक् त्रयम् युञ्ज्यात् स्थूलाणुदीर्घाणां शलाकामन्त्रवृद्धनि मध्योर्ध्ववृत्तदण्डां च मूले चार्धेन्दुसन्निभाम् ३६ कोलास्थिदलतुल्यास्या नासार्शेर्बुद्दाहकृत् अष्टाङ्गुला निम्नमुखास्तिस्रः क्षारौषधक्रमे कनीनीमध्यमानामीनखमानसमैर्मुखैः ३७-३८
transliteration: dvidvārā nalikā picchanalikā vodakodare dhūmabastyādiyantrāṇi nirdiṣṭāni yathāyatham 25 tryaṅgulāsyaṃ bhavecchṛṅgaṃ cūṣaṇe aṣṭādaśāṅgulam agraṃ siddhārthakacchidraṃ sundaraṃ cucukākṛti 26 alābu dvādaśāṅgulaṃ vyāse ṣoḍaśāṅgulam caturaṅgulavṛttāsyaṃ savarti raktakaphāpaham 27 tadvadghaṭī hitā gulmavilayonnamane ca sā 28 śalākākhyāni yantrāṇi nānākarmākṛtīni ca yathāyogapramāṇāni teṣāmeṣaṇakarmaṇi 29 ubhe gaṇḍūpadamukhe srotobhyaḥ śalyahāriṇī masūradalavaktre dve syāttāmaṣṭanavāṅgule 30 śaṅkavaḥ ṣaṭ ubhau teṣāṃ ṣoḍaśadvādaśāṅgulau vyūhane ahaphaṇāvakttau dvau daśadvādaśāṅgulau cālane śarapuṅkhāsyau āhārye baḍiśākṛtī 31 nato agre śaṅkunā tulyo garbhaśaṅkuriti smṛtaḥ aṣṭāṅgulāyatastena mūḍhagarbhaṃ haretstriyāḥ 32 aśmaryaharaṇaṃ sarpaphaṇābaddhakamagrataḥ śarapuṅkhamukhaṃ dantapātanaṃ caturaṅgulam 33 kārpāsavihitoṣṇīṣāḥ śālākāḥ ṣaṭ pramārjane pāyāvāsannadūrārthe dve daśadvādaśāṅgule 34 dve ṣaṭsaptāṅgule ghrāṇe, dve karṇe aṣṭanavāṅgule karṇaśodhanamaśvatthapatraprāntaṃ sruvānanam 35 śalākājāmbavauṣṭhānāṃ kṣāre agnau ca pṛthak trayam yuñjyāt sthūlāṇudīrghāṇāṃ śalākāmantravṛddhani madhyordhvavṛttadaṇḍāṃ ca mūle cārdhendusannibhām 36 kolāsthidalatulyāsyā nāsārśerbuddāh akṛt aṣṭāṅgulā nimnamukhāstisraḥ kṣārauṣadhakrame kanīnīmadhyamānāmīnakhamānasamairmukhaiḥ 37-38
commentary: Nadiyantra for use in Udakodara- ascites shall have two orifices- one at each end or it can be even the tube of a peacocks feather. The Shringa- animal horn useful to suck shall have the orifice of three Angula at its root and that of mustard seed at the tip, eighteen Angula in length. The tip resembles the shape of nipple. Alabu- the hollowed gourd will be twelve Angula in length and eighteen Angula in diameter with a round orifice of four Angula – in which, with a burning wick placed in its interior, useful for extracting Kapha and Raktha- blood. Note – The procedure explained in Alabu yantra is called as cupping. Whenever vitiated blood or pus is to be extracted from a wound / ulcer, Alabu yantra is placed over the affected area and heated from outside. It expands, causing vacuum inside. This causes sucking action and the pus / vitiated blood gets sucked out. Ghati- pot is similar and useful for making the tumors of the abdomen soft and raise it above from its low level. Shalaka yantra – set of instruments with rod like shape. Rod like instruments are of many functions and shapes and size suitable to be purpose for which they are used. Of them, two are for probing, both having their mouth resembling that of an earth worm; two for removing foreign bodies from the channels having their mouths resembling a lentil, one of eight and the other of nine Angula in length. Shanku Yantra – hooks are six, among them two, (16 and 12 Angula in length), their mouth shaped like the hood of a serpent, are meant for joining (the edges of wounds etc); Two more- one of twelve and the other of ten Angula in length, having the mouth resembling a Sharapunkha (bottom of arrow) meant for loosening the hard objects that are to be extracted. The size resembles a fish hook. The hook known as Garbhashanku, is bent in its tip resembling a conch, 18 Angula in length and meant for pulling the impacted foetus in women. Instrument for extracting the stone from the urinary bladder, shall be shaped like the hood of a snake and bent inwards at its tip. Instrument for extracting the tooth should have the shape of Sharapunkha (base of arrow) and is of four Angula – in length. The rod- like instruments meant for clearing sinuses etc. shall have their tip covered with a cap of cotton wool. Two others Nadi yantra (rod like instruments)- one of 10 and other of12 Angula- in length meant for drawing the rectum near – by closing the things and extending it farther. Two other instruments, of six and seven Angula respectively for use in the nose; two of eight and nine Angula for use in the ears. That meant for clearing the ear, with its edge like the leaf of the Ashwattha tree and face resembling a ladle. Jambavoshta- Cylindrical smooth stones- each three in number, thick, thin and long in shape be used for the application of caustic Alkalies and branding by fire – therapies. That meant for use in international Hernia- in the scrotum shall have a round rod, bigger at its middle and upper portion and its root shaped like the half moon. Instrument meant for cauterizing the polyp and tumors of the nose shall have its mouth similar to the cotyledon of the stone of Kola- Jujube fruit. The tree for applying caustic Alkali therapy shall be eight Angula- in length, their mouths –tips resembling the nails of the index, middle and ring finger- in size respectively.

topic_heading: Anu yantra and Functions of Yantra
sanskrit_text: स्वंस्वमुक्तानि यन्त्राणि मेढ्रशुद्ध्यञ्जनादिषु ३९ अनुयन्त्राण्ययस्कान्तरज्ज्वस्त्राश्ममुद्गराः वध्नाश्वजिह्वाबालाश्च शाखानखमुखद्विजाः कालः पाकः करः पदो भयं हर्षश्च, तत्क्रियाः उपायवित्प्रविभजेदालोच्य निपुणं धिया ४० निर्घातनोन्मथनपूरणमार्गशुद्धिसंव्यूहनाहरणबन्धनपीडनानि आचूषणोन्नमननमनचालनभङ्गव्यावर्तनर्जुकरणानि च यन्त्रकर्म ४१ विवर्तते साध्ववगाहते च ग्राह्यं गृहीत्वोद्धरते च यस्मात् । यन्त्रेष्वतः कङ्कमुखं प्रधानं स्थानेषु सर्वेष्वधिकारि यच्च ॥४२ १/२॥
transliteration: svaṃsvamuktāni yantrāṇi meḍhraśuddhy añjanādiṣu 39 anuyantrāṇyayaskāntarajjvastrāśmamudgarāḥ vadhnāśvajihvābālāśca śākhānakhamukhad vijāḥ kālaḥ pākaḥ karaḥ pado bhayaṃ harṣaśca, tatkriyāḥ upāyavitpravibhajedālocya nipuṇaṃ dhiyā 40 nirghātanonmathanapūraṇamārgaśuddhisaṃvyūhanāharaṇabandhanapīḍanāni ācūṣaṇo nnamananamanacālanabhaṅgavyāvartanarjukaraṇāni ca yantrakarma 41 vivartate sādhvavagāhate ca grāhyaṃ gṛhītvoddharate ca yasmāt | yantreṣvataḥ kaṅkamukhaṃ pradhānaṃ sthāneṣu sarveṣvadhikāri yacca ||42 1/2||
commentary: Those meant for clearing the penis / urethra and applying eye salve has been described at relevant places to be continued. Accessory instruments are – the magnet, rope/ thread, cloth, stone, hammer, leather strap, intensive- of animals, tongue, hair, branches of trees, nails mouth, teeth, time, digestion hands, feet, fear and pleasure. They are used judiciously based on the assessment of disease and the patient. Nirghatana- pulling out after crushing, unmathana- pulling out after twisting, Poorana- filling, Marga shuddhi- clearing the passage, Vyuhana- bringing together, Aharana – extracting, Bandhana- binding, Peedana- Rubbing, Achushana – sucking, Unnamana- lifting up, Namana- pushing down, bending down, Chalana- shaking, Bhanga- breaking, Vyavartana- overturning, Rujukarana- straightening etc. are the functions of the Yantras- blunt instruments. Among the blunt instruments Kankamukha Yantra, is the best as it can be twisted easily, dipped deep, can be held firmly, catches the objects firmly and is the authority in all places. It is indispensable.

sanskrit_text: षड्विंशतिः सुकर्मारैर्घटितानि यथाविधि शस्त्राणि रोमवाहीनि बाहुल्येन अङ्गुलानि षट् १ सुरूपाणि सुधाराणि सुग्रहाणि च कारयेत् अकरालानि सुध्मात सुतीक्ष्ण आवर्तिते अयसि २ समाहितमुखाग्राणि नीलाम्भोजच्छवीनि च नामानुगतरूपाणि सदा सन्निहितानि च स्वोन्मानार्ध चतुर्थांश फलानि एकैकशो अपि च प्रायो द्वित्राणि,युञ्जीत तानि स्थानविशेषतः ३-४
transliteration: ṣaḍviṃśatiḥ sukarmārairghaṭitāni yathāvidhi śastrāṇi romavāhīni bāhulyena aṅgulāni ṣaṭ 1 surūpāṇi sudhārāṇi sugrahāṇi ca kārayet akarālāni sudhmāta sutīkṣṇa āvartite ayasi 2 samāhitamukhāgrāṇi nīlāmbhojacchavīni ca nāmānugatarūpāṇi sadā sannihitāni ca svo nmānārdha caturthāṃśa phalāni ekaikaśo api ca prāyo dvitrāṇi, yuñjīta tāni sthānaviśeṣataḥ 3-4
commentary: Shastras- sharp instruments are 26 in number. Shastras should be prepared from skilled metal smiths, as per traditional method of preparing surgical instruments. They should be generally six Angula (fingers breadth)- long, capable of splitting the hair/shaving, good to look at, with sharp edges, good to hold firmly; The Yantras should not be of ugly shape. They should be prepared from well blown – removed of impurities strong steel like iron. The front of their mouth. i.e – the shape edges well hammered – to make them sharp, having the color of the blue lotus, with shape in accordance with their name, always ready at hand for use, their blades- cutting edges being 1/4th, ½th or 1/8th of their own size (total length). Each – instrument two or three in number should be made use as suitable to the place site of operation.

sanskrit_text: मण्डलाग्रं वृद्धिपत्रमुत्पलाध्यर्धधारके सर्पैषण्यौ वेतसाख्यं शरार्यास्यत्रिकूर्चके कुशास्यं साटवदनमन्त्रवक्त्रार्ध चन्द्रके किम् व्रीहिमुखं कुठारी च शलाकाङ्गुलिशस्त्रके बडिशं करपत्राख्यं कर्तरि नखशस्त्रकम् दन्तलेखनकं सूच्यः कूर्चो नाम खजाह्वयम् आरा चतुर्विधाकारा तथा स्यात्कर्णवेधनी ५-८ मण्डलाग्रं फले तेषां तर्जन्यन्तर्नखाकृति लेखने छेदने योज्यं पोथकीशुण्डिकादिषु ९ वृद्धिपत्रं क्षुराकारं छेदभेदपाटने ऋज्वग्रमुन्नते शोफे गम्भीरे च तदन्यथा नताग्रं पृष्ठतो दीर्घह्रस्ववक्त्रं यथाश्रयम् उत्पलाध्यर्धधाराख्ये भेदने छेदने तथा सर्पास्यं घ्राणकर्णार्शः छेदने अर्धाङ्गुलं फलम् गतेरन्वेषणे श्लक्ष्णा गण्डूपदमुखैषणी भेदनार्थे अपरा सूचिमुखा मूलनिविष्टखा वेतसं व्यधने स्राव्ये शरार्यास्यत्रिकूर्चके कुशाटावदने स्राव्ये द्व्यङ्गुलं स्यात्तयोः फलम् १०-१३
transliteration: maṇḍalāgraṃ vṛddhipatramutpalādhyardhadhārake sarpaiṣaṇyau vetasākhyaṃ śarāryāsyatrikūrcake kuśāsyaṃ sāṭavadanamantravaktrārdha candrake kim vrīhimukhaṃ kuṭhārī ca śalākāṅguliśastra ke baḍiśaṃ karapatrākhyaṃ kartari nakhaśastrakam dantalekhanakaṃ sūcyaḥ kūrco nāma khajāhvayam ārā caturvidhākārā tathā syātkarṇavedhanī 5-8 maṇḍalāgraṃ phale teṣāṃ tarjanyantarnakhākṛti lekhane chedane yojyaṃ pothakīśuṇḍikādiṣu 9 vṛddhipatraṃ kṣurākāraṃ chedabhedapāṭane ṛjvagramunnate śophe gambhīre ca tadanyathā natāgraṃ pṛṣṭhato dīrghah rasvavaktraṃ yathāśrayam utpalādhyardhadhārākhye bhedane chedane tathā sarpāsyaṃ ghrāṇakarṇārśaḥ chedane ardhaṅgulaṃ phalam gateranveṣaṇe ślakṣṇā gaṇḍūpadamukhaiṣaṇī bhedanārthe aparā sūcimukhā mūlaniviṣṭakhā vetasaṃ vyadhane srāvye śarāryāsyatrikūrcake kuśāṭāvadane srāvye dvyaṅgulaṃ syāttayoḥ phalam 10-13
commentary: Mandalagra, Vriddhiptra, Uttpala Patra, Adhyardha Dhara, Sarpa Mukha, Eshani, Vetasa Patra, Sarari Mukha, Trikurchaka, Kushapatra, Atavadana Atimukhi, Antrarvaktra, Ardha chandraka, Vrihimukha, Kuthari, Shalaka, Anguli Shastra, Badisa, Karapatra, Kartari, Nakha Shastra, Danta lekhanaka, Suchi, Koorcha, Khaja, the four kinds of Ara, and Karna vedhanaka- are the names of the twenty six sharp instruments. Mandalagra Shastra- knife with round edge at its tip has its edge in the shape of nail of the index finger, to be made use of for scraping and cutting-excision, in diseases like Pothaki- cyst in the eyelid, Shundika- Tonsils etc. Vridhipatra- Scalpel is shaped like a boarders knife- Razor, useful for cutting, excision, splitting, incision and tearing/ separating, it, with a straight edge, is for use in elevated – bulging swelling, the same with its tip bent backwards, long or short edge for use in deep seated swelling. Utpalapatra and Ardha dhara- lancets are for the purpose of splitting and cutting. Sarpyasya- Sarpamukha- serpent bladed scalpel is meant for cutting – excision of polyps in the nose and ears and has an edge of half Angula. Eshani- sharp probe meant for exploring sinuses, is smooth and shaped like the mouth of an earthworm. Another kind of Eshani- probe meant for splitting, has its blade like a needle, with a slit- hole at its root. Vetasapatra is for puncturing; Shararimukhi- shaped like a heron's beak's kind of scissors and Trikuracaka – three spiked Brush like instrument are meant for draining out liquids. Kushapatra- Razor resembling Blade of Kusha grass and Atimukha- razor resembling the beak of a hawk are meant for draining, edge is two Angula – in length.

topic_heading: Antramukha, Vrihimukha, Kuthari, Shalaka, Anguli Shastra, Badisha, Karapatra, Kartari, Nakha Shastra, Danta Lekhanaka, Suchi, Koorcha, Khaja, Ara
sanskrit_text: तद्वदन्तर्मुखं तस्य फलमध्यर्धमङ्गुलम् अर्धचन्द्राननं चैतत् तथा अध्यर्धाङ्गुलं फले व्रीहिवक्त्रं प्रयोज्यं च तच्छिरोदरयोर्व्यधे १४ पृथुः कुठारी गोदन्तसदृशार्धाङ्गुलानना तयोर्ध्वदण्डया विध्येदुपरिस्थितां सिराम् १५ ताम्री शलाका द्विमुखी मुखे कुरुबकाकृतिः लिङ्गनाशं तथा विध्येत् १६ मुद्रिकानिर्गतमुखं फले त्वर्धाङ्गुलायतम् तत्प्रदेशिन्यग्रपर्वप्रमाणार्पणमुद्रिकम् सूत्रबद्धं गलस्रोतोरोगच्छेदनभेदने १७ ग्रहणे शुण्डिकार्मादेर्बडिशं सुनताननम् छेदे अस्थ्ना करपत्रं तु खरधारं दशाङ्गुलम् विस्तारे सूक्ष्मदन्तं सुसरुबन्धनम् १८ स्नायुसूत्रकचच्छेदे कर्तरी कर्तरीनिमा वक्रर्जुधारं द्विमुखं नखशस्त्रं नवाङ्गुलम् सूक्ष्मशल्योद्धृतिच्छेदभेदप्रच्छानलेखने १९ एकधारं चतुष्कोणं प्रबद्धाकृति चैकतः दन्तलेखनकं तेन शोधयेद्दन्तशर्कराम् २० वृत्ता गूढदृढाः पाशे तिस्रः सूच्योऽत्र सीवने मांसलानां प्रदेशानां त्र्यस्रा त्र्यङ्गुलमायता अल्पमांसास्थिसन्धिस्थव्रणानां द्व्यङ्गुलमायता २१ व्रीहिवक्त्रा धनुर्वक्रा पक्वामाशयमर्मसु सा सार्धद्व्यङ्गुला सर्ववृत्तास्ताश्चतुरङ्गुलाः कूर्चो वृत्तैकपीठस्थाः सप्ताष्टौ वा सुबन्धनाः स योज्यो नीलिकाव्यङ्गकेशशातेषु कुट्टने २२ अर्धाङ्गुलमुखैर्वृत्तैरष्टाभिः कण्टकैः खजः पाणिभ्यां मथ्यमानेन घ्राणात्तेन हरेदसृक् २३ व्यधनं कर्णपालीनां यूथिकामुकुलाननम् आरा अर्धाङ्गुलवृत्तस्या तत्प्रवेशा तथोर्ध्वतः चतस्रा, तया विध्येच्छोफं पक्वामसंशये कर्णपालीं च बहलाम् बहलायाश्च शस्यते सूची त्रिभागसुषिरः त्र्यङ्गुला कर्णवेधनी २४-२६
transliteration: tadvadantarmukhaṃ tasya phalamadhyardhamaṅgulam ardha candrānanaṃ caitat tathā adhyardhāṅgulaṃ phale vrīhivaktraṃ prayojyaṃ ca tacchirodarayorvyadhe 14 pṛthuḥ kuṭhārī godantasadṛśārdhāṅgulānanā tayordhvadaṇḍayā vidhyetuparisthitāṃ sirām 15 tāmrī śalākā dvimukhī mukhe kurubakākṛtiḥ liṅganāśaṃ tathā vidhyet 16 mudrikānirgatamukhaṃ phale tvarthāṅgulāyatam tatpradeśinyagraparvapramāṇārpaṇamudrikam sūtrabaddhaṃ galasrotorogacchedanabhedane 17 grahaṇe śuṇḍikārmāderbaḍiśaṃ sunatānanam cede asthnā karapatraṃ tu kharadhāraṃ daśāṅgulam vistāre sūkṣmadantaṃ susarubandhanam 18 snāyusūtrakacacchede kartarī kartarīnimā vakrarjudhāraṃ dvimukhaṃ nakhaśastraṃ navāṅgulam sūkṣmaśalyoddhṛticchedabhedapracchānalekhane 19 ekadhāraṃ catuṣkoṇaṃ prabaddhākṛti caikataḥ dantalekhanakaṃ tena śodhayed dantaśarkarām 20 vṛttā gūḍhadṛḍhāḥ pāśe tisraḥ sūcyo'tra sīvane māṃsalānāṃ pradeśānāṃ tryasrā tryaṅgulamāyatā alpa māṃsāsthisandhisthavraṇānāṃ dvyaṅgulamāyatā 21 vrīhivaktrā dhanurvakrā pakvāmāśayamarmasu sā sārdhadvyaṅgulā sarvavṛttāstāścaturaṅgulāḥ kūrco vṛttaikapīṭhasthāḥ saptāṣṭau vā subandhanāḥ sa yojyo nīlikāvyaṅgakeśaśāteṣu kuṭṭane 22 ardhaṅgulamukhairvṛttairaṣṭābhiḥ kaṇṭakaiḥ khajaḥ pāṇibhyāṃ mathyamānena ghrāṇāttena haredasṛk 23 vyadhanaṃ karṇapālīnāṃ yūthikāmukulānanam ārā ardhaṅgulavṛttasyā tatprav eśā tathordhvataḥ catasrā, tayā vidhyecchophaṃ pakvāmasaṃśaye karṇapālīṃ ca bahalām bahalāyāśca śasyate sūcī tribhāgasuṣiraḥ tryaṅgulā karṇavedhanī 24-26
commentary: Antramukha – is meant for draining, its edges – 1.5 Angula in length and Shaped like half moon.
